3.2.2.s: athaitad vātsapram etena vai vatsaprīr bhālandano 'gneḥ priyaṃ dhāmārādhnot tad agner evaitena priyaṃ dhāma rādhnoty āgāmukam enaṃ priyaṃ bhavati vatsapriyaṃ vai bhālandanam āśayo 'dhyavadan stenā iti sa etat sūktam apaśyat te nādhivādam apājayat tenāpacitim agachat tad adhivādam evaitenāpajayaty apacitim eva gachati dvādaśabhir upatiṣṭhate dvādaśa māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaram evāptvāvarunddhe triṣṭubho bhavantīndriyasyāvaruddhyay anyedyuḥ prakrāmayaty anyedyur upatiṣṭhate yogakṣemaṃ vā etat prajānāṃ dādhāra tasmād yāyāvarā anyāḥ prajāḥ kṣemyā anyā atha yat prakramyopatiṣṭhate tasmād yāyāvaraḥ kṣemyam abhiprayāti tasmād yāyāvarasya kṣemyo 'nnaṃ babhūva yad ahaś ceṣyamāṇaḥ syāt tad ahar ubhayaṃ samasyet pra ca krāmed upa ca tiṣṭheta yogakṣemaṃ vā etad annādyaṃ yajamāno bhrātṛvyasya vṛṅkta ud u tvā viśve devā iti viśve hīdaṃ devāḥ smo yan manuṣyā agne bharantu cittibhir iti yasmā eva cittāyāgnir ādhīyate tenainaṃ cittena samardhayati pred agne jyotiṣmān yāhīti jyotiṣaivainaṃ samardhayitvā pravāpayaty akrandad agniḥ stanayann iva dyaur ity anubrūyād yady akṣa utkṣveded īśvaro vā eṣa utkṣvedan yajamānasya prajāṃ paśūn nikṣvadas tat kraditam evāsyākar atho śamayitvaivāśiṣam āśāste samidhāgniṃ duvasyateti gāyatryā brāhmaṇasyādadhyād gāyatro hi brāhmaṇas triṣṭubhā rājanyasya traiṣṭubho hi rājanyo dvābhyāṃ gāyatrībhyāṃ vaiśyasya ye hi dve gāyatryau sā jagaty atho brahmaṇe vā etad viśam annaṃ karoti yadi bhasma pratipūryetāpsu praveśayed āpo vā agner yoniḥ sva evainad yonau dadhāti purīṣaṃ kuryāt paśukāmasya paśavo vai purīṣaṃ paśumān bhavatīṣṭakā vā saṃyuyāt tenāsya sarvā āgneyīr iṣṭakā bhavanty ūrjā vā eṣa paśubhir utsīdant sahotsīdati punar ūrjā nivartasveti tad ūrjam eva paśūn punar avarunddhe bodhā me asya vacaso yaviṣṭheti bodhadvatībhyām upatiṣṭhate tasmāt prajāḥ suptvā punaḥ prabudhyante dvābhyām upatiṣṭhate dvipād yajamānaḥ pratiṣṭhityai ||
3.2.2.d: अथैतद् वात्सप्रम् एतेन वै वत्सप्रीर् भालन्दनो ऽग्नेः प्रियं धामाराध्नोत् तद् अग्नेर् एवैतेन प्रियं धाम राध्नोत्य् आगामुकम् एनं प्रियं भवति वत्सप्रियं वै भालन्दनम् आशयो ऽध्यवदन् स्तेना इति स एतत् सूक्तम् अपश्यत् ते नाधिवादम् अपाजयत् तेनापचितिम् अगछत् तद् अधिवादम् एवैतेनापजयत्य् अपचितिम् एव गछति द्वादशभिर् उपतिष्ठते द्वादश मासाः संवत्सरः संवत्सरम् एवाप्त्वावरुन्द्धे त्रिष्टुभो भवन्तीन्द्रियस्यावरुद्ध्यय् अन्येद्युः प्रक्रामयत्य् अन्येद्युर् उपतिष्ठते योगक्षेमं वा एतत् प्रजानां दाधार तस्माद् यायावरा अन्याः प्रजाः क्षेम्या अन्या अथ यत् प्रक्रम्योपतिष्ठते तस्माद् यायावरः क्षेम्यम् अभिप्रयाति तस्माद् यायावरस्य क्षेम्यो ऽन्नं बभूव यद् अहश् चेष्यमाणः स्यात् तद् अहर् उभयं समस्येत् प्र च क्रामेद् उप च तिष्ठेत योगक्षेमं वा एतद् अन्नाद्यं यजमानो भ्रातृव्यस्य वृङ्क्त उद् उ त्वा विश्वे देवा इति विश्वे हीदं देवाः स्मो यन् मनुष्या अग्ने भरन्तु चित्तिभिर् इति यस्मा एव चित्तायाग्निर् आधीयते तेनैनं चित्तेन समर्धयति प्रेद् अग्ने ज्योतिष्मान् याहीति ज्योतिषैवैनं समर्धयित्वा प्रवापयत्य् अक्रन्दद् अग्निः स्तनयन्न् इव द्यौर् इत्य् अनुब्रूयाद् यद्य् अक्ष उत्क्ष्वेदेद् ईश्वरो वा एष उत्क्ष्वेदन् यजमानस्य प्रजां पशून् निक्ष्वदस् तत् क्रदितम् एवास्याकर् अथो शमयित्वैवाशिषम् आशास्ते समिधाग्निं दुवस्यतेति गायत्र्या ब्राह्मणस्यादध्याद् गायत्रो हि ब्राह्मणस् त्रिष्टुभा राजन्यस्य त्रैष्टुभो हि राजन्यो द्वाभ्यां गायत्रीभ्यां वैश्यस्य ये हि द्वे गायत्र्यौ सा जगत्य् अथो ब्रह्मणे वा एतद् विशम् अन्नं करोति यदि भस्म प्रतिपूर्येताप्सु प्रवेशयेद् आपो वा अग्नेर् योनिः स्व एवैनद् योनौ दधाति पुरीषं कुर्यात् पशुकामस्य पशवो वै पुरीषं पशुमान् भवतीष्टका वा संयुयात् तेनास्य सर्वा आग्नेयीर् इष्टका भवन्त्य् ऊर्जा वा एष पशुभिर् उत्सीदन्त् सहोत्सीदति पुनर् ऊर्जा निवर्तस्वेति तद् ऊर्जम् एव पशून् पुनर् अवरुन्द्धे बोधा मे अस्य वचसो यविष्ठेति बोधद्वतीभ्याम् उपतिष्ठते तस्मात् प्रजाः सुप्त्वा पुनः प्रबुध्यन्ते द्वाभ्याम् उपतिष्ठते द्विपाद् यजमानः प्रतिष्ठित्यै ॥

3.2.3.s: apeta vīta vi ca sarpatātā ity āha yamadevatyo vā ayaṃ loko yamo 'muṣya lokasyādhipatyam ānaśa yad yamād devayajanam aniryācyāgniṃ cinvītāyamadevatyo 'syāgniḥ syād asvargyo yad āhādād idaṃ yamo 'vasānaṃ pṛthivyā akrann imaṃ pitaro lokam asā iti yamād vā etenāsyā devayajanaṃ nirayāciṣṭa smṛte devayajane 'gniṃ cinute yamadevatyo 'syāgnir bhavati svarga ud u ghnanti yad evāsyā ayajñiyam amedhyaṃ tad udghnanti vyāmamātram udghnanty etāvad vai puruṣe vīryaṃ vīryasammite cīyate 'tho etāvān vai puruṣe mahimā mahimno 'varuddhyay avokṣati yad evāsyā udghnantaḥ krūram akraṃs tad akrūram akas tañ śamayaty atho āpo vā agner yoniḥ sva eva yonau cīyate 'gner bhasmāsy agneḥ purīṣam asīti sikatā nivapaty agner vā etad vaiśvānarasya bhasma yat sikatā sva eva bhasmaṃś cīyate yonir vai sikatā retā ūṣā yat sikatā nyupyoṣān nivapati yonau vā etad reto dadhāti tasmād yonau reto hitaṃ tasmād yone retaḥ prajāyate prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tā vā ūṣebhya eva yoner asṛjata prajananaṃ vā ūṣāḥ prajanane vā etad agniś cīyata ime vai sahāstāṃ te viyatī abrūtām astu nau priyaṃ dhāma sahety āpo vā asyā yajñiyā medhyās tā amūr ūṣā amuṣyā yajñiyā medhyās ta ime yad āpaś coṣāś ca bhavanti yad evainayor yajñiyaṃ medhyaṃ tad avarunddhe 'tho anayor evainaṃ priye dhāman nidhatte saṃjñānaṃ vā ūṣā ubhaye vā etān paśavo 'bhisaṃjānate ye grāmyāḥ paśavo ye cāraṇyā ubhaye hainaṃ paśavo 'bhisaṃjānate catasraḥ prācīḥ sādayati catvāri vai chandāṃsi chandobhir vai devāḥ svargaṃ lokam āyaṃs te diśā ākramanta tā avlīyanta tā etābhir adṛṃhan yad etā upadhīyante diśāṃ dhṛtyai paśavo vā iṣṭakā gārhapatyaṃ vai paśavo 'nūpatiṣṭhante dve samīcī purastād upadadhāti dve samīcī paścād ubhayata evāsmai samīcaḥ paśūn upadadhāti paśūnāṃ parigṛhītyay aṣṭopadadhāty aṣṭākṣarā gāyatrī gāyatro 'gnir yāvān evāgnis taṃ cinuta ekaviṃśatiḥ kāryā pratiṣṭhityai pratiṣṭhā hy ekaviṃśo 'tho ekaviṃśatividho hi gārhapatyas tricitikaḥ kāryas trayo vā ime lokā imān eva lokān āpnoti pañcacitikaḥ kāryaḥ pāṅkto yajño yāvān eva yajñas tam ālabdha caturbhiḥ saṃnivapati catvāri vai chandāṃsi chandobhir eva saṃnivapaty atho brahma vai chandāṃsi brahmaṇaiva saṃnivapati kṣatraṃ vā eṣo 'gnīnāṃ yaś cīyate kṣatraṃ ya ukhyo brahma yajur yad yajuṣā saṃnivapati brahmaṇā vā etat kṣatraṃ saṃnayati tasmād brahmaṇā kṣatraṃ saṃ caiti vi ca dvau vā etau vyāghrau saṃ padyete tā īśvarā aśāntau yajamānaṃ hiṃsitor yad āha bhavataṃ naḥ samanasau samokasau sacetasā arepasā iti śamayaty eva śānta eva nyupyate yajamānasyāhiṃsāyay ṛtubhir vai pṛthivyā vīryam udyataṃ tad ṛtubhiḥ punar vimucyate yad āha prajāpatir viśvakarmā vimuñcatv iti prajāpatir evaināṃ viśvakarmā vimuñcati ||
3.2.3.d: अपेत वीत वि च सर्पताता इत्य् आह यमदेवत्यो वा अयं लोको यमो ऽमुष्य लोकस्याधिपत्यम् आनश यद् यमाद् देवयजनम् अनिर्याच्याग्निं चिन्वीतायमदेवत्यो ऽस्याग्निः स्याद् अस्वर्ग्यो यद् आहादाद् इदं यमो ऽवसानं पृथिव्या अक्रन्न् इमं पितरो लोकम् असा इति यमाद् वा एतेनास्या देवयजनं निरयाचिष्ट स्मृते देवयजने ऽग्निं चिनुते यमदेवत्यो ऽस्याग्निर् भवति स्वर्ग उद् उ घ्नन्ति यद् एवास्या अयज्ञियम् अमेध्यं तद् उद्घ्नन्ति व्याममात्रम् उद्घ्नन्त्य् एतावद् वै पुरुषे वीर्यं वीर्यसम्मिते चीयते ऽथो एतावान् वै पुरुषे महिमा महिम्नो ऽवरुद्ध्यय् अवोक्षति यद् एवास्या उद्घ्नन्तः क्रूरम् अक्रंस् तद् अक्रूरम् अकस् तञ् शमयत्य् अथो आपो वा अग्नेर् योनिः स्व एव योनौ चीयते ऽग्नेर् भस्मास्य् अग्नेः पुरीषम् असीति सिकता निवपत्य् अग्नेर् वा एतद् वैश्वानरस्य भस्म यत् सिकता स्व एव भस्मंश् चीयते योनिर् वै सिकता रेता ऊषा यत् सिकता न्युप्योषान् निवपति योनौ वा एतद् रेतो दधाति तस्माद् योनौ रेतो हितं तस्माद् योने रेतः प्रजायते प्रजापतिः प्रजा असृजत ता वा ऊषेभ्य एव योनेर् असृजत प्रजननं वा ऊषाः प्रजनने वा एतद् अग्निश् चीयत इमे वै सहास्तां ते वियती अब्रूताम् अस्तु नौ प्रियं धाम सहेत्य् आपो वा अस्या यज्ञिया मेध्यास् ता अमूर् ऊषा अमुष्या यज्ञिया मेध्यास् त इमे यद् आपश् चोषाश् च भवन्ति यद् एवैनयोर् यज्ञियं मेध्यं तद् अवरुन्द्धे ऽथो अनयोर् एवैनं प्रिये धामन् निधत्ते संज्ञानं वा ऊषा उभये वा एतान् पशवो ऽभिसंजानते ये ग्राम्याः पशवो ये चारण्या उभये हैनं पशवो ऽभिसंजानते चतस्रः प्राचीः सादयति चत्वारि वै छन्दांसि छन्दोभिर् वै देवाः स्वर्गं लोकम् आयंस् ते दिशा आक्रमन्त ता अव्लीयन्त ता एताभिर् अदृंहन् यद् एता उपधीयन्ते दिशां धृत्यै पशवो वा इष्टका गार्हपत्यं वै पशवो ऽनूपतिष्ठन्ते द्वे समीची पुरस्ताद् उपदधाति द्वे समीची पश्चाद् उभयत एवास्मै समीचः पशून् उपदधाति पशूनां परिगृहीत्यय् अष्टोपदधात्य् अष्टाक्षरा गायत्री गायत्रो ऽग्निर् यावान् एवाग्निस् तं चिनुत एकविंशतिः कार्या प्रतिष्ठित्यै प्रतिष्ठा ह्य् एकविंशो ऽथो एकविंशतिविधो हि गार्हपत्यस् त्रिचितिकः कार्यस् त्रयो वा इमे लोका इमान् एव लोकान् आप्नोति पञ्चचितिकः कार्यः पाङ्क्तो यज्ञो यावान् एव यज्ञस् तम् आलब्ध चतुर्भिः संनिवपति चत्वारि वै छन्दांसि छन्दोभिर् एव संनिवपत्य् अथो ब्रह्म वै छन्दांसि ब्रह्मणैव संनिवपति क्षत्रं वा एषो ऽग्नीनां यश् चीयते क्षत्रं य उख्यो ब्रह्म यजुर् यद् यजुषा संनिवपति ब्रह्मणा वा एतत् क्षत्रं संनयति तस्माद् ब्रह्मणा क्षत्रं सं चैति वि च द्वौ वा एतौ व्याघ्रौ सं पद्येते ता ईश्वरा अशान्तौ यजमानं हिंसितोर् यद् आह भवतं नः समनसौ समोकसौ सचेतसा अरेपसा इति शमयत्य् एव शान्त एव न्युप्यते यजमानस्याहिंसायय् ऋतुभिर् वै पृथिव्या वीर्यम् उद्यतं तद् ऋतुभिः पुनर् विमुच्यते यद् आह प्रजापतिर् विश्वकर्मा विमुञ्चत्व् इति प्रजापतिर् एवैनां विश्वकर्मा विमुञ्चति ॥
3.2.3.m: "Go away, disperse, and glide apart from here!" he says. / This world indeed belongs to Yama as deity. / Yama attained overlordship over that world. / If he were to pile the fire without begging the place of sacrifice from Yama, his fire would not belong to Yama as deity, [and] would not be heavenly. / When he says: / "Yama gave this resting place of the earth; the fathers made this world for him," / by this, indeed, he begs the place of sacrifice from Yama for him. / On the remembered place of sacrifice he piles the fire; his fire belongs to Yama as deity in the heavenly world. / And they dig out. / Whatsoever of it is unfit for sacrifice and unholy, that they dig out. / They dig out a fathom in measure. / So much indeed is the virility in a man. / It is piled commensurate with virility. / Moreover, so much indeed is the greatness in a man, / for the obtaining of greatness. / He sprinkles it down. / Whatsoever was cruel that they did in digging it out, that he makes un-cruel; / he appeases it. / Moreover, water indeed is the womb of fire. / In its own womb indeed it is piled. / "You are the ash of Agni, you are the loose earth of Agni," saying [this], he scatters sand. / That sand indeed is the ash of Agni Vaiśvānara. / In his own ash indeed it is piled. / The sand indeed is the womb; / the saline earth is semen. / When, having scattered sand, he scatters saline earth, / in the womb indeed he places semen. / Therefore semen is placed in the womb; / therefore semen is born from the womb. / Prajāpati created creatures; / he created them indeed from the saline earth, from the womb. / Saline earth indeed is procreation; / in procreation indeed fire is piled. / These two indeed were together. / Being separated, they said: / "Let our dear domain be together." / The waters of this [earth] indeed are worthy of sacrifice and fit for offering; / they are those [above]. / The saline earths of that [heaven] are worthy of sacrifice and fit for offering; / they are these [below]. / In that there are waters and saline earths, / whatsoever of the two is worthy of sacrifice and fit for offering, that he secures. / Moreover, in the dear domain of these two he places it. / Saline earth indeed is concord. / Both [kinds of] cattle indeed acknowledge this: those cattle which are of the village and those which are of the wilderness. / Both cattle indeed acknowledge him. / He sets down four facing east. / There are indeed four meters. / By the meters indeed the gods went to the heavenly world. / They strode out to the directions. / They collapsed. / They made them firm with these [bricks]. / In that these are laid down, / [it is] for the supporting of the directions. / Bricks indeed are cattle. / Cattle indeed attend upon the Gārhapatya. / He lays down two facing each other in front, two facing each other behind. / From both sides indeed he lays down cattle facing each other for him, / for the encompassing of cattle. / He lays down eight. / The Gāyatrī has eight syllables. / Agni belongs to the Gāyatra. / As great as Agni is, so much he piles. / Twenty-one are to be made, / for firm standing, / for the twenty-first is a firm standing. / Moreover, the Gārhapatya is twenty-one-fold. / It is to be made with three layers. / Three indeed are these worlds. / He reaches these very worlds. / It is to be made with five layers. / Fivefold is the sacrifice. / As great as the sacrifice is, so much he seizes. / He scatters together with four [verses]. / There are indeed four meters. / With the meters indeed he scatters together. / Moreover, the meters are sacred power. / By sacred power indeed he scatters together. / The [fire] that is piled is the royal power among the fires; / the [fire] of the pan is the royal power; / the yajus formula is sacred power. / When he scatters together with a yajus formula, / he unites royal power with sacred power. / Therefore royal power unites and separates through sacred power. / These two indeed come together as two tigers. / If unappeased, they are capable of harming the sacrificer. / When he says: / "Become concordant for us, of the same dwelling, like-minded, without blemish," / he appeases [them]. / Only appeased is it scattered down, / for the non-harming of the sacrificer. / By the seasons indeed the virility of the earth was raised up. / By the seasons it is released again. / When he says: / "Let Prajāpati Viśvakarman release [it]," / Prajāpati Viśvakarman indeed releases it.

3.2.4.s: athaitā nairṛtīs tisras tuṣapakvā bhavanty etad vai nairṛtam annasya yat tuṣāḥ kṛṣṇā bhavanty etad dhi nirṛtyā rūpam etāṃ diśaṃ haranty eṣā hi nirṛtyā dik tāḥ svakṛtā iriṇe parācīr nidadhāty etad vai nirṛtigṛhītaṃ pṛthivyā nirṛtigṛhīta eva nirṛtiṃ niravadayate prāṇam evāsya prathamayā muñcaty apānaṃ dvitīyayā vyānaṃ tṛtīyayātho tryakṣaro vai puruṣo yāvān eva puruṣas taṃ nirṛtyāḥ pāpmano muñcati nirṛtir vai karmaṇa upadraṣṭrikā tāṃ vā etat svena bhāgadheyena śamayitvātha savitṛprasūto 'gniṃ cinute yaṃ te devī nirṛtir ābabandheti jālam iṣṭakāsv adhyasyati nirṛtipāśam evonmuñcata ātmano 'hiṃsāyai || yad asya pāre rajaso mahaś citraṃ jyotir ajātaya | tan naḥ parṣad ati dviṣo 'gne vaiśvānaraḥ || svāhety apaḥ pariṣiñcan paryeti nirṛtyā ananvavāyāya bhūtyai namā ity uktvāvartate bhūtir eva bhūtvāvartata ātmano 'hiṃsāyay anapekṣamāṇā āyanti nirṛtyā ananvavāyāya parogoṣṭhaṃ mārjayante parogoṣṭham eva nirṛtiṃ niravadayanta indriyena vā eṣa vīryeṇa vyṛdhyate yo nairṛtīr upadhatte niveśanaḥ saṃgamano vasūnām ity aindryā gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhata indriyeṇaivātmānaṃ samardhayati triṣṭubhopatiṣṭhata ojo vai vīryaṃ triṣṭub ojasy eva vīrye pratitiṣṭhati gārhapatyo 'gre cīyate pratiṣṭhityai gārhapatye vai devāḥ pratiṣṭhāya prāñcaḥ svargaṃ lokam abhijayanta āyan yāvān puruṣa ūrdhvabāhus tāvatā veṇunā vimimīta etāvad vai puruṣe vīryaṃ vīryeṇaiva vimimīte 'tho etāvān vai puruṣe mahimā mahimno 'varuddhyai yo vai vanaspatīnāṃ phalagrahitamaḥ sa eṣāṃ vīryavattamo venur vai vanaspatīnāṃ phalagrahitamaḥ sa eṣāṃ vīryavattamo 'nnaṃ vai phalam annam arko 'rko 'gnir arkeṇa vā etad annam arkam agniṃ vimimīte sapta puruṣān pramimīte saptabhya eva puruṣebhyo lokaṃ vindaty ā saptamāt puruṣād annādo bhavaty aratnimātraṃ pakṣayor atyupadadhāti pakṣaṃbṛhad dhi vayaḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ kṛṣati ṣāḍ vā ṛtava ṛtubhir eva kṛṣatīttham abhyāvartanta kṛṣaty eṣā hi devānām āvṛd atho amuṣya vā etad ādityasyāvṛtam anuparyāvartante tisrastisraḥ sītāḥ saṃpādayati trivṛd dhy agnir dvādaśa sītā bhavanti dvādaśa māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsarasya vā eṣa vidhām anuvidhīyata iyaṃ vā abibhed agnir mātidhakṣyatīti yat kṛṣaty asyā vā etad dviguṇaṃ kriyate 'natidāhāyātho pṛthivyā vā etad dviguṇenāgner vīryam udyachanta etāṃ diśam utsṛjanty eṣā hi devānāṃ dig atho svargam evaināṃ lokam anūtsṛjanti ||
3.2.4.d: अथैता नैरृतीस् तिस्रस् तुषपक्वा भवन्त्य् एतद् वै नैरृतम् अन्नस्य यत् तुषाः कृष्णा भवन्त्य् एतद् धि निरृत्या रूपम् एतां दिशं हरन्त्य् एषा हि निरृत्या दिक् ताः स्वकृता इरिणे पराचीर् निदधात्य् एतद् वै निरृतिगृहीतं पृथिव्या निरृतिगृहीत एव निरृतिं निरवदयते प्राणम् एवास्य प्रथमया मुञ्चत्य् अपानं द्वितीयया व्यानं तृतीययाथो त्र्यक्षरो वै पुरुषो यावान् एव पुरुषस् तं निरृत्याः पाप्मनो मुञ्चति निरृतिर् वै कर्मण उपद्रष्ट्रिका तां वा एतत् स्वेन भागधेयेन शमयित्वाथ सवितृप्रसूतो ऽग्निं चिनुते यं ते देवी निरृतिर् आबबन्धेति जालम् इष्टकास्व् अध्यस्यति निरृतिपाशम् एवोन्मुञ्चत आत्मनो ऽहिंसायै ॥ यद् अस्य पारे रजसो महश् चित्रं ज्योतिर् अजातय । तन् नः पर्षद् अति द्विषो ऽग्ने वैश्वानरः ॥ स्वाहेत्य् अपः परिषिञ्चन् पर्येति निरृत्या अनन्ववायाय भूत्यै नमा इत्य् उक्त्वावर्तते भूतिर् एव भूत्वावर्तत आत्मनो ऽहिंसायय् अनपेक्षमाणा आयन्ति निरृत्या अनन्ववायाय परोगोष्ठं मार्जयन्ते परोगोष्ठम् एव निरृतिं निरवदयन्त इन्द्रियेन वा एष वीर्येण व्यृध्यते यो नैरृतीर् उपधत्ते निवेशनः संगमनो वसूनाम् इत्य् ऐन्द्र्या गार्हपत्यम् उपतिष्ठत इन्द्रियेणैवात्मानं समर्धयति त्रिष्टुभोपतिष्ठत ओजो वै वीर्यं त्रिष्टुब् ओजस्य् एव वीर्ये प्रतितिष्ठति गार्हपत्यो ऽग्रे चीयते प्रतिष्ठित्यै गार्हपत्ये वै देवाः प्रतिष्ठाय प्राञ्चः स्वर्गं लोकम् अभिजयन्त आयन् यावान् पुरुष ऊर्ध्वबाहुस् तावता वेणुना विमिमीत एतावद् वै पुरुषे वीर्यं वीर्येणैव विमिमीते ऽथो एतावान् वै पुरुषे महिमा महिम्नो ऽवरुद्ध्यै यो वै वनस्पतीनां फलग्रहितमः स एषां वीर्यवत्तमो वेनुर् वै वनस्पतीनां फलग्रहितमः स एषां वीर्यवत्तमो ऽन्नं वै फलम् अन्नम् अर्को ऽर्को ऽग्निर् अर्केण वा एतद् अन्नम् अर्कम् अग्निं विमिमीते सप्त पुरुषान् प्रमिमीते सप्तभ्य एव पुरुषेभ्यो लोकं विन्दत्य् आ सप्तमात् पुरुषाद् अन्नादो भवत्य् अरत्निमात्रं पक्षयोर् अत्युपदधाति पक्षंबृहद् धि वयः षड्भिः कृषति षाड् वा ऋतव ऋतुभिर् एव कृषतीत्थम् अभ्यावर्तन्त कृषत्य् एषा हि देवानाम् आवृद् अथो अमुष्य वा एतद् आदित्यस्यावृतम् अनुपर्यावर्तन्ते तिस्रस्तिस्रः सीताः संपादयति त्रिवृद् ध्य् अग्निर् द्वादश सीता भवन्ति द्वादश मासाः संवत्सरः संवत्सरस्य वा एष विधाम् अनुविधीयत इयं वा अबिभेद् अग्निर् मातिधक्ष्यतीति यत् कृषत्य् अस्या वा एतद् द्विगुणं क्रियते ऽनतिदाहायाथो पृथिव्या वा एतद् द्विगुणेनाग्नेर् वीर्यम् उद्यछन्त एतां दिशम् उत्सृजन्त्य् एषा हि देवानां दिग् अथो स्वर्गम् एवैनां लोकम् अनूत्सृजन्ति ॥
3.2.4.m:
Now, these are the [bricks] belonging to Nirṛti.
There are three, baked with chaff.
What is chaff, that indeed belongs to Nirṛti among food.
They are black,
for this is the form of Nirṛti.
They carry [them] in this direction,
for this is the direction of Nirṛti.
He deposits them, turned away, in a naturally cleft hollow,
for this is the Nirṛti-seized [part] of the earth.
In the Nirṛti-seized [part] alone he appeases Nirṛti.
By the first he releases his out-breath,
by the second his down-breath,
by the third his through-breath.
Moreover, man indeed consists of three syllables;
as great as man is, so much he releases from Nirṛti's evil.
Nirṛti is indeed the onlooker of the rite.
Having appeased her with her own portion, then, impelled by Savitṛ, he piles the fire.
"Which the goddess Nirṛti has bound for you," saying [this], he throws a net upon the bricks.
He unlooses the fetter of Nirṛti,
for the non-injury of himself.
"The great, wonderful light, on the further side of this space, for the unborn, / let that, Agni Vaiśvānara, ferry us across our enemies, svāhā!" Saying [this], sprinkling water, he walks around,
to avoid the pursuit of Nirṛti.
Saying, "Homage to Prosperity!" he turns back.
Having become prosperity itself, he turns back,
for the non-injury of himself.
They come back without looking around,
to avoid the pursuit of Nirṛti.
They cleanse themselves beyond the cattle-pen;
beyond the cattle-pen they appease Nirṛti.
He who lays down the [bricks] belonging to Nirṛti is deprived of faculty and vigor.
"Dwelling-place, gatherer of riches," with this verse addressed to Indra he attends upon the Gārhapatya [fire].
He enriches himself with faculty.
He attends [upon it] with a triṣṭubh;
the triṣṭubh is force and vigor;
he firmly stands in force and vigor.
The Gārhapatya [fire] is piled first,
for firm standing.
Having firmly stood upon the Gārhapatya, the gods went forward, conquering the heavenly world.
He measures with a bamboo as tall as a man with arms upstretched;
so much indeed is the vigor in a man;
he measures by vigor itself.
Moreover, so much is the greatness in a man,
for the securing of greatness.
Whichever is the most fruitful among trees, that is the most vigorous of them;
the bamboo is the most fruitful among trees;
it is the most vigorous of them.
Fruit is food,
food is the Arka,
the Arka is Agni;
with the Arka he measures food, the Arka, Agni.
He measures out seven men;
he obtains a world for seven men;
down to the seventh man he becomes an eater of food.
He lays down [extra bricks] on the two wings by a cubit in measure;
for a bird is large-winged.
He plows with six [oxen];
six are the seasons;
with the seasons he plows.
Turning about thus,
he plows;
for this is the turning-around of the gods.
Moreover, they turn following the course of that sun.
He accomplishes three furrows each [time];
for threefold is Agni.
There are twelve furrows;
twelve months are a year;
he is measured out according to the measure of the year.
This [earth] feared:
"Agni will burn me excessively."
When he plows,
a double layer of this [earth] is made,
for non-excessive burning.
Moreover, with a double layer of earth they sustain the vigor of Agni.
They leave off in this direction,
for this is the direction of the gods.
Moreover, they release it toward the heavenly world.

3.2.5.s: kṛṣṭe vapati kṛṣṭe hy oṣadhayaḥ kṣepiṣṭhaṃ pratitiṣṭhanty annasyānnasya vapaty oṣadhīnām ṛgbhir brahma vā ṛg brahmaṇaivāsmā annādyam avarunddhe caturdaśabhir vapati dvādaśa māsāḥ saṃvatsaro 'tha ya ete caturdaśe ahorātre evaite tat saṃvatsareṇa ca vāvāsmā etad ahorātrābhyāṃ cānnādyam avarunddhe 'nnaṃ vai phalam annam arko 'rko 'gnir arkeṇa vā etad annam arkam agniṃ vapati yasyānnasya nivapati yat tasyāśnīyād yāny avaruddhāni tair vyadhyetedhme tasyāpikuryād atho tan manasā dhyāyet tenaiva tad avarunddhe yadi sarvaṃ na saṃvinded yavān madhūdyutān vaped yad yavā grāmyaṃ tenānnādyam avarunddhe yan madhv āraṇyaṃ tena tenaiva tad ubhayam avarunddhe 'thaite saṃbhārā digbhyo vā etat pṛthivyā ūrjaṃ saṃbharaty ūrjy agniś cīyate yāṃ janatāṃ kāmayeta kṣodhukā syād itīṣam ūrjam aham ita ādīti tasyā ardhād ādadīta kṣodhukā ha sā janatā bhavati kāmaṃ kāmadughe dhukṣvety abhimṛśati tenāsya sarvā iṣṭakāḥ kāmadughā bhavanty uttaravediṃ nivapaty uttaravedim ity evāsyāgniś cīyate 'tho yajñaparuṣo 'nantarhityay agnir vā eṣa nyupyate yad uttaravedir yad uttaravediṃ nyupyāgniṃ cinoty agnau vā etad agniś cīyate 'gne tava śravo vapā iti sikatā nivapaty etā vai vaiśvānarīr iṣṭakā aparimitā etad agner aparimitaṃ cīyate 'gner vā etad vaiśvānarasya sūktam eṣā vā agneḥ priyā tanūr yad vaiśvānaraḥ priyāyāṃ vā etat tanvām agniś cīyate satanūr arko nidhīyate lomaśaṃ vā etac chandaḥ paśavyam ūnātiriktaṃ prajananāyāśītyakṣaram etena vai devāḥ svargaṃ lokam āyaṃs tad asyāśītyakṣaratvaṃ samudraṃ vā etac chando yoniḥ samudraḥ somo retodhā yat saumībhyāṃ vyūhati yonau vā etad reto dadhāti tasmād yonau reto hitam āpyānavatī bhavatas tasmād yonau retā āpyāyate chandobhir vā agnir uttaravedim abhiprahriyate yā agnau prahriyamāṇe 'nvāhus tāṃ tarhi manasā dhyāyec chandobhir evainam uttaravedim abhipraharati manasānvāhāniruktam iva hy etad avyāvṛttaṃ vyāvṛtaṃ pāpmanā bhrātṛvyeṇa gachaty aśvaṃ purastān nayanti rakṣasām apahatyay ākramayanti ya evainena bhrātṛvyaḥ sadṛṅ taṃ vajreṇāvabādhante prāñcaṃ prakramayanti ya evainaṃ bhrātṛvyo 'ti taṃ vajreṇa praṇudate pratyañcam abhyāvartayanti ya evainaṃ bhrātṛvyo 'nu taṃ vajreṇa pratinudate tad bhrātṛvyasya vā eṣa vinodaḥ kṛṣṇo vai bhūtvāgnir aśvaṃ prāviśat sa etad agachad yatra mṛgaśapho yad aśvam ākramayanti yad evātrāgner nyaktaṃ tasyāvaruddhyai ||
3.2.5.d: कृष्टे वपति कृष्टे ह्य् ओषधयः क्षेपिष्ठं प्रतितिष्ठन्त्य् अन्नस्यान्नस्य वपत्य् ओषधीनाम् ऋग्भिर् ब्रह्म वा ऋग् ब्रह्मणैवास्मा अन्नाद्यम् अवरुन्द्धे चतुर्दशभिर् वपति द्वादश मासाः संवत्सरो ऽथ य एते चतुर्दशे अहोरात्रे एवैते तत् संवत्सरेण च वावास्मा एतद् अहोरात्राभ्यां चान्नाद्यम् अवरुन्द्धे ऽन्नं वै फलम् अन्नम् अर्को ऽर्को ऽग्निर् अर्केण वा एतद् अन्नम् अर्कम् अग्निं वपति यस्यान्नस्य निवपति यत् तस्याश्नीयाद् यान्य् अवरुद्धानि तैर् व्यध्येतेध्मे तस्यापिकुर्याद् अथो तन् मनसा ध्यायेत् तेनैव तद् अवरुन्द्धे यदि सर्वं न संविन्देद् यवान् मधूद्युतान् वपेद् यद् यवा ग्राम्यं तेनान्नाद्यम् अवरुन्द्धे यन् मध्व् आरण्यं तेन तेनैव तद् उभयम् अवरुन्द्धे ऽथैते संभारा दिग्भ्यो वा एतत् पृथिव्या ऊर्जं संभरत्य् ऊर्ज्य् अग्निश् चीयते यां जनतां कामयेत क्षोधुका स्याद् इतीषम् ऊर्जम् अहम् इत आदीति तस्या अर्धाद् आददीत क्षोधुका ह सा जनता भवति कामं कामदुघे धुक्ष्वेत्य् अभिमृशति तेनास्य सर्वा इष्टकाः कामदुघा भवन्त्य् उत्तरवेदिं निवपत्य् उत्तरवेदिम् इत्य् एवास्याग्निश् चीयते ऽथो यज्ञपरुषो ऽनन्तर्हित्यय् अग्निर् वा एष न्युप्यते यद् उत्तरवेदिर् यद् उत्तरवेदिं न्युप्याग्निं चिनोत्य् अग्नौ वा एतद् अग्निश् चीयते ऽग्ने तव श्रवो वपा इति सिकता निवपत्य् एता वै वैश्वानरीर् इष्टका अपरिमिता एतद् अग्नेर् अपरिमितं चीयते ऽग्नेर् वा एतद् वैश्वानरस्य सूक्तम् एषा वा अग्नेः प्रिया तनूर् यद् वैश्वानरः प्रियायां वा एतत् तन्वाम् अग्निश् चीयते सतनूर् अर्को निधीयते लोमशं वा एतच् छन्दः पशव्यम् ऊनातिरिक्तं प्रजननायाशीत्यक्षरम् एतेन वै देवाः स्वर्गं लोकम् आयंस् तद् अस्याशीत्यक्षरत्वं समुद्रं वा एतच् छन्दो योनिः समुद्रः सोमो रेतोधा यत् सौमीभ्यां व्यूहति योनौ वा एतद् रेतो दधाति तस्माद् योनौ रेतो हितम् आप्यानवती भवतस् तस्माद् योनौ रेता आप्यायते छन्दोभिर् वा अग्निर् उत्तरवेदिम् अभिप्रह्रियते या अग्नौ प्रह्रियमाणे ऽन्वाहुस् तां तर्हि मनसा ध्यायेच् छन्दोभिर् एवैनम् उत्तरवेदिम् अभिप्रहरति मनसान्वाहानिरुक्तम् इव ह्य् एतद् अव्यावृत्तं व्यावृतं पाप्मना भ्रातृव्येण गछत्य् अश्वं पुरस्तान् नयन्ति रक्षसाम् अपहत्यय् आक्रमयन्ति य एवैनेन भ्रातृव्यः सदृङ् तं वज्रेणावबाधन्ते प्राञ्चं प्रक्रमयन्ति य एवैनं भ्रातृव्यो ऽति तं वज्रेण प्रणुदते प्रत्यञ्चम् अभ्यावर्तयन्ति य एवैनं भ्रातृव्यो ऽनु तं वज्रेण प्रतिनुदते तद् भ्रातृव्यस्य वा एष विनोदः कृष्णो वै भूत्वाग्निर् अश्वं प्राविशत् स एतद् अगछद् यत्र मृगशफो यद् अश्वम् आक्रमयन्ति यद् एवात्राग्नेर् न्यक्तं तस्यावरुद्ध्यै ॥
3.2.5.m:
He sows on cultivated [ground];
for on cultivated [ground] plants establish themselves most swiftly.
He sows of each kind of food, of the plants, with ṛc verses.
The ṛc, indeed, is the sacred word.
By means of the sacred word alone he secures food for him.
He sows with fourteen [verses].
Twelve months are the year.
Then those which are the fourteenth, those indeed are day and night.
Thus, indeed, through the year and through the two, day and night, he secures food for him.
Food, indeed, is the fruit.
Food is the arka [plant / song].
The arka is Agni.
By means of the arka, indeed, he thus sows food, the arka, Agni.
Of whatever food he sows, if he were to eat of that, he would be pierced by those which have been secured.
He should add of it to the kindling wood;
moreover, he should meditate upon it with the mind.
By that alone he secures it.
If he should not find everything, he should sow barley mixed with honey.
Because [there is] barley, through that he secures domestic food;
because [there is] honey, through that [he secures] wild [food].
By that alone he secures both.
Now, these are the requisites.
From the quarters, indeed, he thus collects the nourishment of the earth.
In nourishment the fire is piled.
Regarding whatever people he should desire: 'May they be hungry,' [saying,] 'Nourishment and sap I take from here,' he should take from their region;
hungry indeed does that people become.
'Yield your desire, O wish-granting [cow]!' he touches [the earth].
Thereby all his bricks become wish-granting.
He pours out the high altar.
Only as the high altar, indeed, is his fire piled.
Moreover, [it is] for the non-interruption of the joints of the sacrifice.
Agni, indeed, is this poured out, which is the high altar.
When, having poured out the high altar, he piles the fire,
upon Agni, indeed, Agni is thus piled.
'O Agni, your fame...' with this he pours out sand.
These, indeed, are the unlimited Vaiśvānara bricks.
This unlimited [form] of Agni is piled.
This, indeed, is the hymn of Agni Vaiśvānara.
This, indeed, is Agni's dear body, which is Vaiśvānara.
In the dear body, indeed, Agni is thus piled;
possessed of a body, the arka is deposited.
Hairy, indeed, is this metre, rich in cattle, deficient and redundant,
for procreation.
It has eighty syllables.
By this, indeed, the gods went to the heavenly world.
That is its eighty-syllabled nature.
An ocean, indeed, is this metre.
The ocean is the womb.
Soma is the depositor of semen.
When he separates with two verses addressed to Soma,
in the womb, indeed, he thus deposits semen;
therefore semen is deposited in the womb.
They possess swelling;
therefore semen swells in the womb.
With metres, indeed, Agni is brought forward to the high altar.
Those which they recite when Agni is being brought forward, those he should then meditate on with the mind.
With metres alone he brings him forward to the high altar.
He recites with the mind.
For this is as it were unexpressed, undivided.
He attains separation from evil, from his rival.
They lead a horse in front,
for the smiting away of the Rakṣases.
They cause [it] to step forward.
Whatever rival is his equal, him they thrust down with the thunderbolt.
They cause [it] to step eastward.
Whatever rival exceeds him, him he thrusts away with the thunderbolt.
They turn [it] round facing westward.
Whatever rival follows him, him he thrusts back with the thunderbolt.
That, indeed, is this driving away of the rival.
Having become black, Agni indeed entered the horse.
He went to this where a wild beast's hoof [is].
When they cause the horse to step on [it],
whatever hidden mark of Agni is here, [it is] for the securing of that.

3.2.6.s: tapo yonir asīti puṣkaraparṇam upadadhāti yonir vā eṣo 'gner yat puṣkaraparṇaṃ nābhir vadhakaḥ sayonir eva sanābhiś cīyata iyaṃ vā abibhed agnir mātidhakṣyatīti yat puṣkaraparṇam upadadhāty asyā anatidāhāyādhastānnābhi sādayaty oṣadhīnāṃ pratiṣṭhityay atho ye 'psv agnayas tān evāvarunddhe prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata yāḥ purā brahmaṇo 'sṛjata tābhir nārādhnod atha yā brahmamukhā asṛjata tābhir arādhnod yad brahma jajñānaṃ prathamaṃ purastād iti rukmam upadadhāty ṛddhyay ṛdhnoty evātho mithunatvāya na pṛthivyām agniś cetavyo nāntarikṣe na divīty āhur amṛtaṃ vai hiraṇyam amṛte vā etad agniś cīyate śmaśānacito vā ete cīyante cityāṃcityāṃ hiraṇyaśakalam upāsyati tena vā eṣo 'śmaśānacit tena svargo 'thaiṣa puruṣo hiraṇyayo yajamānalokam evaiṣa dādhāraiṣa ha tv eva yajamāno 'gnināmuṣmiṃl loke samyaṅ yasyaiṣa upadhīyate 'tho madhye jyotir eva cīyate drapsaś caskanda pṛthivīm anu dyām ity abhimṛśati hotrāsv evainaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayaty athaitāni sarpanāmāni mṛtyur vai sarpanāmāni yad upadadhyāt pramāyukaḥ syāt tasmād anudiśati some vā ekā tviṣir vyāghra ekā sarpa ekā tā evāvarunddhe vāmadevasya rākṣoghnena vyāghārayaty etena vai vāmadevaḥ kusitāyyāḥ śirā ādīpayad rakṣasām apahatyai pañcabhir vyāghārayati pāṅkto yajño yāvān eva yajñas tam ālabdhātho yāvān eva yajñas tasmād rakṣāṃsy apahanty athaite srucau kārṣmaryamayīṃ dakṣiṇataḥ sādayati rakṣasām apahatyai dakṣiṇato vai devānāṃ yajñaṃ rakṣāṃsy ajighāṃsaṃs tāni kārṣmaryeṇaivāpāghnata yat kārṣmaryamayīṃ dakṣiṇataḥ sādayati rakṣasāmapahatyai ghṛtasya pūrṇā bhavaty eṣā vā agneḥ priyā tanūr yad ghṛtaṃ priyayaivainaṃ tanvā samardhayati gāyatryā sādayati tejo vai gāyatrī brahmavarcasaṃ teja eva brahmavarcasam avarunddha audumbarīm uttarataḥ sādayati dadhnaḥ pūrṇām ūrg vā udumbaro 'nnaṃ dadhy ūrjy evāsyānnaṃ dadhāti triṣṭubhā sādayaty ojo vai vīryaṃ triṣṭub oja eva vīryam avarunddhe pūrṇe sādayaty akṣite yajamānalokam upatiṣṭhete mūrdhanvatībhyāṃ sādayati mūrdhanyo 'sānīti virājy agniś cetavyā ity āhuḥ srucau vai virājau yat srucā upadadhāti virāji vā etad agniś cīyate 'thaiṣā svayamātṛṇṇeyaṃ vai prathamā svayamātṛṇṇāntarikṣaṃ dvitīyāsau tṛtīyemān eva lokān upadhatte 'śvam upaghrāyya sādayati prajāpaticita evāsya bhavaty atho prāṇānām utsṛṣṭyai bhūr asīti prācīm udūhed yady enaṃ bhrātṛvyo 'tīva syād bhūmir asīti pratīcīṃ yady anv aditir asi bhūmir asīti tiraścīṃ yadi sadṛṅṅ iyaṃ vā aditir anayā vā etad yajamāno bhrātṛvyaṃ prabhūtaṃ praṇudate 'nayā pratinudate 'nayā vinudate tad bhrātṛvyasya vā eṣa vinodaḥ kāṇḍātkāṇḍāt prarohantīti dūrveṣṭakām upadadhāty oṣadhīnāṃ pratiṣṭhityai kāṇḍātkāṇḍād dhy eṣā pratitiṣṭhati paśavo vā iṣṭakā na vai paśavā āyavase ramante yad dūrveṣṭakām upadadhāty āyatanam iva vā etat kriyate paśūnāṃ yatyay athaiṣā vāmabhṛd dviryajur yajamānalokam anyena dādhāra bhrātṛvyalokam anyena vṛṅkta etayā vai devā asurāṇāṃ vāmaṃ paśūn avṛñjata tad vāmabhṛto vāmabhṛttvaṃ chandāṃsi vai devānāṃ vāmaṃ paśavaś chandāṃsy evaitayā vāmaṃ paśūn yajamāno bhrātṛvyasya vṛṅkte 'thaite retaḥsicav iyaṃ virāḍ asu svarāḍ asā eva retaḥ siñcatīyaṃ prajanayaty agnir atyannādo bhavati yasyaite upadhīyete yadi putrī cinvīta prathamāyāṃ cityām anyām upadadhyād uttamāyām anyāṃ retasaḥ siktasya parigṛhītyai yady aputraḥ prathamāyāṃ cityām ubhe upadheye samyañcau hi bhūtvā retaḥ siñcataḥ ||
3.2.6.d: तपो योनिर् असीति पुष्करपर्णम् उपदधाति योनिर् वा एषो ऽग्नेर् यत् पुष्करपर्णं नाभिर् वधकः सयोनिर् एव सनाभिश् चीयत इयं वा अबिभेद् अग्निर् मातिधक्ष्यतीति यत् पुष्करपर्णम् उपदधात्य् अस्या अनतिदाहायाधस्तान्नाभि सादयत्य् ओषधीनां प्रतिष्ठित्यय् अथो ये ऽप्स्व् अग्नयस् तान् एवावरुन्द्धे प्रजापतिः प्रजा असृजत याः पुरा ब्रह्मणो ऽसृजत ताभिर् नाराध्नोद् अथ या ब्रह्ममुखा असृजत ताभिर् अराध्नोद् यद् ब्रह्म जज्ञानं प्रथमं पुरस्ताद् इति रुक्मम् उपदधात्य् ऋद्ध्यय् ऋध्नोत्य् एवाथो मिथुनत्वाय न पृथिव्याम् अग्निश् चेतव्यो नान्तरिक्षे न दिवीत्य् आहुर् अमृतं वै हिरण्यम् अमृते वा एतद् अग्निश् चीयते श्मशानचितो वा एते चीयन्ते चित्यांचित्यां हिरण्यशकलम् उपास्यति तेन वा एषो ऽश्मशानचित् तेन स्वर्गो ऽथैष पुरुषो हिरण्ययो यजमानलोकम् एवैष दाधारैष ह त्व् एव यजमानो ऽग्निनामुष्मिंल् लोके सम्यङ् यस्यैष उपधीयते ऽथो मध्ये ज्योतिर् एव चीयते द्रप्सश् चस्कन्द पृथिवीम् अनु द्याम् इत्य् अभिमृशति होत्रास्व् एवैनं प्रतिष्ठापयत्य् अथैतानि सर्पनामानि मृत्युर् वै सर्पनामानि यद् उपदध्यात् प्रमायुकः स्यात् तस्माद् अनुदिशति सोमे वा एका त्विषिर् व्याघ्र एका सर्प एका ता एवावरुन्द्धे वामदेवस्य राक्षोघ्नेन व्याघारयत्य् एतेन वै वामदेवः कुसिताय्याः शिरा आदीपयद् रक्षसाम् अपहत्यै पञ्चभिर् व्याघारयति पाङ्क्तो यज्ञो यावान् एव यज्ञस् तम् आलब्धाथो यावान् एव यज्ञस् तस्माद् रक्षांस्य् अपहन्त्य् अथैते स्रुचौ कार्ष्मर्यमयीं दक्षिणतः सादयति रक्षसाम् अपहत्यै दक्षिणतो वै देवानां यज्ञं रक्षांस्य् अजिघांसंस् तानि कार्ष्मर्येणैवापाघ्नत यत् कार्ष्मर्यमयीं दक्षिणतः सादयति रक्षसामपहत्यै घृतस्य पूर्णा भवत्य् एषा वा अग्नेः प्रिया तनूर् यद् घृतं प्रिययैवैनं तन्वा समर्धयति गायत्र्या सादयति तेजो वै गायत्री ब्रह्मवर्चसं तेज एव ब्रह्मवर्चसम् अवरुन्द्ध औदुम्बरीम् उत्तरतः सादयति दध्नः पूर्णाम् ऊर्ग् वा उदुम्बरो ऽन्नं दध्य् ऊर्ज्य् एवास्यान्नं दधाति त्रिष्टुभा सादयत्य् ओजो वै वीर्यं त्रिष्टुब् ओज एव वीर्यम् अवरुन्द्धे पूर्णे सादयत्य् अक्षिते यजमानलोकम् उपतिष्ठेते मूर्धन्वतीभ्यां सादयति मूर्धन्यो ऽसानीति विराज्य् अग्निश् चेतव्या इत्य् आहुः स्रुचौ वै विराजौ यत् स्रुचा उपदधाति विराजि वा एतद् अग्निश् चीयते ऽथैषा स्वयमातृण्णेयं वै प्रथमा स्वयमातृण्णान्तरिक्षं द्वितीयासौ तृतीयेमान् एव लोकान् उपधत्ते ऽश्वम् उपघ्राय्य सादयति प्रजापतिचित एवास्य भवत्य् अथो प्राणानाम् उत्सृष्ट्यै भूर् असीति प्राचीम् उदूहेद् यद्य् एनं भ्रातृव्यो ऽतीव स्याद् भूमिर् असीति प्रतीचीं यद्य् अन्व् अदितिर् असि भूमिर् असीति तिरश्चीं यदि सदृङ्ङ् इयं वा अदितिर् अनया वा एतद् यजमानो भ्रातृव्यं प्रभूतं प्रणुदते ऽनया प्रतिनुदते ऽनया विनुदते तद् भ्रातृव्यस्य वा एष विनोदः काण्डात्काण्डात् प्ररोहन्तीति दूर्वेष्टकाम् उपदधात्य् ओषधीनां प्रतिष्ठित्यै काण्डात्काण्डाद् ध्य् एषा प्रतितिष्ठति पशवो वा इष्टका न वै पशवा आयवसे रमन्ते यद् दूर्वेष्टकाम् उपदधात्य् आयतनम् इव वा एतत् क्रियते पशूनां यत्यय् अथैषा वामभृद् द्विर्यजुर् यजमानलोकम् अन्येन दाधार भ्रातृव्यलोकम् अन्येन वृङ्क्त एतया वै देवा असुराणां वामं पशून् अवृञ्जत तद् वामभृतो वामभृत्त्वं छन्दांसि वै देवानां वामं पशवश् छन्दांस्य् एवैतया वामं पशून् यजमानो भ्रातृव्यस्य वृङ्क्ते ऽथैते रेतःसिचव् इयं विराड् असु स्वराड् असा एव रेतः सिञ्चतीयं प्रजनयत्य् अग्निर् अत्यन्नादो भवति यस्यैते उपधीयेते यदि पुत्री चिन्वीत प्रथमायां चित्याम् अन्याम् उपदध्याद् उत्तमायाम् अन्यां रेतसः सिक्तस्य परिगृहीत्यै यद्य् अपुत्रः प्रथमायां चित्याम् उभे उपधेये सम्यञ्चौ हि भूत्वा रेतः सिञ्चतः ॥
3.2.6.m:
With "Thou art heat, the womb," he places the lotus leaf.
For the womb of Agni is this, namely the lotus leaf.
The bādhaka is the navel.
Possessing its womb, possessing its navel it is piled.
This [earth] indeed feared:
"Agni will burn me overmuch."
In that he places the lotus leaf,
[it is] so that she will not be burnt overmuch.
He sets it down with the navel beneath,
for the establishment of the plants;
moreover, what fires are in the waters, those alone he secures.
Prajāpati created creatures.
Those which he created prior to the sacred word, through them he did not prosper.
Then those which had the sacred word as their head he created; through them he prospered.
In that he places the gold plate with "The sacred word that was first born in the east,"
[it is] for prosperity.
He prospers indeed;
moreover, [it is] for pair-formation.
"Agni is not to be piled on the earth, nor in the atmosphere, nor in heaven," they say.
Gold, indeed, is immortality.
On immortality, indeed, Agni is thus piled.
These indeed are piled as pile-layers on a burial mound;
in layer after layer he throws down a gold chip.
By that, indeed, this one is not a pile-layer on a burial mound;
by that [the fire] leads to heaven.
Now this golden man:
he indeed upholds the world of the sacrificer.
For this sacrificer indeed unites with Agni in that world, for whom this is placed.
Moreover, in the middle light alone is piled.
With "A drop has fallen down upon the earth, along heaven," he touches [it].
In the hotrā invocations alone he establishes him.
Now these names of the serpents:
the names of the serpents are death.
If he were to place [bricks with them], he would be liable to die.
Therefore he assigns [them] without placing.
In Soma, indeed, is one brilliance;
in the tiger, one;
in the serpent, one.
Those alone he secures.
He sprinkles around with the rākṣoghna [hymn] of Vāmadeva.
By this, indeed, Vāmadeva kindled the heads of Kusitāyī,
for the smiting away of the Rakṣases.
He sprinkles around with five [verses].
The sacrifice is fivefold;
as great as the sacrifice is, him he has grasped;
moreover, from as great as the sacrifice is, he smites away the Rakṣases.
Now these two offering ladles:
he sets down the one made of kārṣmarya on the south,
for the smiting away of the Rakṣases.
From the south, indeed, the Rakṣases sought to strike the sacrifice of the gods;
them they smote away with the kārṣmarya alone.
In that he sets down the one made of kārṣmarya on the south,
[it is] for the smiting away of the Rakṣases.
It is full of ghee.
Ghee is this dear body of Agni.
With [his] dear body alone he causes him to prosper.
He sets it down with the Gāyatrī.
The Gāyatrī is brilliance [and] spiritual lustre;
brilliance [and] spiritual lustre he secures.
He sets down the one made of udumbara on the north, full of curd.
The udumbara is vigor;
curd is food.
In vigor alone he places food for him.
He sets it down with the Triṣṭubh.
The Triṣṭubh is force [and] valor;
force [and] valor he secures.
He sets down two full ones;
undiminished they attend upon the world of the sacrificer.
He sets them down with two [verses] containing "head",
[thinking:] "May I be at the head."
"Agni is to be piled on the Virāj," they say.
The two offering ladles, indeed, are the two Virājs.
In that he places the two offering ladles,
on the Virāj indeed Agni is thus piled.
Now this naturally perforated [brick]:
this [earth], indeed, is the first naturally perforated [brick];
the atmosphere is the second;
that [heaven] is the third.
These worlds indeed he places.
Having made the horse sniff it, he sets it down;
it becomes for him piled by Prajāpati;
moreover, [it is] for the emission of the vital breaths.
With "Thou art Bhūḥ" he should push it up toward the east if a rival should surpass him;
with "Thou art the earth" toward the west if behind;
with "Thou art Aditi, thou art the earth" across if equal.
This [earth] indeed is Aditi;
by this, indeed, the sacrificer thrusts away a rival who has prevailed;
by this he thrusts him back;
by this he thrusts him apart.
That, indeed, is this repulse of the rival.
With "Growing sprout by sprout" he places the dūrvā-brick,
for the establishment of the plants;
for sprout by sprout does this [grass] establish itself.
Bricks, indeed, are cattle;
cattle do not delight without pasture.
In that he places the dūrvā-brick,
this is done, as it were, as an abode
for the going of the cattle.
Now this vāmabhṛt [brick] has two yajus formulas;
with the one he upholds the world of the sacrificer, with the other he excludes the world of the rival.
By this, indeed, the gods excluded the desirable wealth, the cattle, of the Asuras.
That is the vāmabhṛt-nature of the vāmabhṛt.
The metres, indeed, are the desirable wealth, the cattle, of the gods;
the metres indeed, the desirable wealth, the cattle, the sacrificer excludes for his rival by this.
Now these two seed-pourers [bricks]:
this [earth] is Virāj;
that [heaven] is Svarāj.
That one indeed pours seed;
this one brings forth.
Agni becomes an excessive consumer of food for whom these two are placed.
If one possessing a son should pile [the fire], he should place one in the first layer,
the other in the highest [layer],
for the grasping of the seed poured out.
If one is without a son, both are to be placed in the first layer;
for having become united they pour seed.

3.2.7.s: athaitā viśvajyotiṣa eṣu vā etal lokeṣu jyotiṣmantam agniṃ nidhatte 'tho prāṇānāṃ vidhṛtyay athaiṣā tryālikhiteme vai lokās tryālikhitemān eva lokān upādhatta ubhaye vā etām upādadhata devāś ca vā asurāś copariṣṭāllakṣmāṇaṃ devā upādadhatādhastāllakṣmāṇam asurās tato devā abhavan parāsurā upariṣṭāllakṣmāṇam upadadhīta bhrātṛvyavān yo vāsya priyaḥ syāt tasya bhavaty ātmanā parāsya bhrātṛvyo bhavaty eṣa vā asapatneṣṭakāsapatno bhavati ya etām upadhatte 'tho devalakṣmaṃ vā eṣā devalakṣmam evopadhatte yā sokhāyā adhi mṛd uñśiṣyate tasyā etāṃ kuryāt tenāsya sarvā āgneyīr iṣṭakā bhavanty athaiṣa kūrmaḥ śmaśānacito vā ete cīyante jīvaḥ kūrma upadheyas tena vā eṣo 'śmaśānacit tenotpātī paśūnāṃ vā eṣa medha etaṃ vai medhaṃ paśyanta enaṃ paśavo 'muṣmiṃl loka upatiṣṭhante pratyañcaṃ sādayati pratyañco hi paśavo medham upatiṣṭhate dyāvāpṛthivīyayā sādayati dyāvāpṛthivī hi paśavo 'nūpatiṣṭhante paśubhir evainaṃ samyañcaṃ dadhāti viṣṇor nābhyām agniś cetavyā ity āhuḥ prādeśamātram ulūkhalaṃ kāryam etāvān vai viṣṇur viṣṇor vā etan nābhyām agnis cīyata ūrjy agniś cetavyā ity āhur ūrg vā udumbaro yad audumbaram ulūkhalaṃ bhavaty ūrji vā etad agniś cīyate vaiṣṇavyā sādayati vaiṣṇavaṃ hy ulūkhalaṃ svayaiva devatayāthaiṣokhā pṛthivyā vā etad ojo vīryaṃ saṃbhriyata ojo vā etad vīryaṃ madhyato 'gner dhīyate 'tho madhye jyotir eva cīyate yad riktām avekṣeta kṣodhuko yajamānaḥ syād atha yat pūrṇām avekṣate tathā hākṣodhuko bhavati sikatābhiḥ pūrayitavyāgner vā etad vaiśvānarasya bhasma yat sikatāḥ svenaivaināṃ bhasmanā prīṇāti dadhnaḥ pūrayitavyorg vai dadhy ūrjam evāvarunddhe hṛtasya pūrayitavyaiṣā vā agneḥ priyā tanūr yad ghṛtaṃ priyayaivainaṃ tanvā samardhayati madhoḥ pūrayitavyā hāsya prajāyāṃ madhavyo jāyate vyṛdhyaindriyāṇi vai paśuśīrṣāṇy ayajñiyāny amedhyāni yac chidreṣu hiraṇyaśakalāny apy asyatīndriyeṇaivaināni vīryeṇa samardhayati medhyāny enāni yajñiyāni karoty ardhaṃ vai puruṣaḥ sahasrasya yachanty ardham itare paśavas tasmād etan madhyata upadadhāty abhitā itarāṇi paśoḥ savīryatvāyātho sāyatanatvāya yaṃ kāmayeta paśumānt syād iti tasya samīcīnāni paśuśīrṣāṇy upadadhyāt samīca evāsmai paśūn upadadhāti paśumān bhavaty atha yaṃ kāmayetāpaśuḥ syād iti tasya viṣūcīnāni paśuśīrṣāṇy upadadhyād viṣūca evāsmai paśūn upadadhāty apaśur bhavaty etā vai sāhasrīr iṣṭakāḥ paśviṣṭakās tāḥ somadakṣaḥ kauśreyo vidāṃcakāra tāḥ śyāparṇāyopadadhau sa sahasraṃ paśūn prāpa pra sahasraṃ paśūn āpnoti yasyaitā upadhīyante yaviṣṭho vai nāmaiṣo 'gnis tasmāc cinvītāntarā na vyetavai yad vīyāt prāṇān asya yuvetotsargair upatiṣṭhata āraṇyān eva paśūñ śucam anūtsṛjati ||
3.2.7.d: अथैता विश्वज्योतिष एषु वा एतल् लोकेषु ज्योतिष्मन्तम् अग्निं निधत्ते ऽथो प्राणानां विधृत्यय् अथैषा त्र्यालिखितेमे वै लोकास् त्र्यालिखितेमान् एव लोकान् उपाधत्त उभये वा एताम् उपादधत देवाश् च वा असुराश् चोपरिष्टाल्लक्ष्माणं देवा उपादधताधस्ताल्लक्ष्माणम् असुरास् ततो देवा अभवन् परासुरा उपरिष्टाल्लक्ष्माणम् उपदधीत भ्रातृव्यवान् यो वास्य प्रियः स्यात् तस्य भवत्य् आत्मना परास्य भ्रातृव्यो भवत्य् एष वा असपत्नेष्टकासपत्नो भवति य एताम् उपधत्ते ऽथो देवलक्ष्मं वा एषा देवलक्ष्मम् एवोपधत्ते या सोखाया अधि मृद् उञ्शिष्यते तस्या एतां कुर्यात् तेनास्य सर्वा आग्नेयीर् इष्टका भवन्त्य् अथैष कूर्मः श्मशानचितो वा एते चीयन्ते जीवः कूर्म उपधेयस् तेन वा एषो ऽश्मशानचित् तेनोत्पाती पशूनां वा एष मेध एतं वै मेधं पश्यन्त एनं पशवो ऽमुष्मिंल् लोक उपतिष्ठन्ते प्रत्यञ्चं सादयति प्रत्यञ्चो हि पशवो मेधम् उपतिष्ठते द्यावापृथिवीयया सादयति द्यावापृथिवी हि पशवो ऽनूपतिष्ठन्ते पशुभिर् एवैनं सम्यञ्चं दधाति विष्णोर् नाभ्याम् अग्निश् चेतव्या इत्य् आहुः प्रादेशमात्रम् उलूखलं कार्यम् एतावान् वै विष्णुर् विष्णोर् वा एतन् नाभ्याम् अग्निस् चीयत ऊर्ज्य् अग्निश् चेतव्या इत्य् आहुर् ऊर्ग् वा उदुम्बरो यद् औदुम्बरम् उलूखलं भवत्य् ऊर्जि वा एतद् अग्निश् चीयते वैष्णव्या सादयति वैष्णवं ह्य् उलूखलं स्वयैव देवतयाथैषोखा पृथिव्या वा एतद् ओजो वीर्यं संभ्रियत ओजो वा एतद् वीर्यं मध्यतो ऽग्नेर् धीयते ऽथो मध्ये ज्योतिर् एव चीयते यद् रिक्ताम् अवेक्षेत क्षोधुको यजमानः स्याद् अथ यत् पूर्णाम् अवेक्षते तथा हाक्षोधुको भवति सिकताभिः पूरयितव्याग्नेर् वा एतद् वैश्वानरस्य भस्म यत् सिकताः स्वेनैवैनां भस्मना प्रीणाति दध्नः पूरयितव्योर्ग् वै दध्य् ऊर्जम् एवावरुन्द्धे हृतस्य पूरयितव्यैषा वा अग्नेः प्रिया तनूर् यद् घृतं प्रिययैवैनं तन्वा समर्धयति मधोः पूरयितव्या हास्य प्रजायां मधव्यो जायते व्यृध्यैन्द्रियाणि वै पशुशीर्षाण्य् अयज्ञियान्य् अमेध्यानि यच् छिद्रेषु हिरण्यशकलान्य् अप्य् अस्यतीन्द्रियेणैवैनानि वीर्येण समर्धयति मेध्यान्य् एनानि यज्ञियानि करोत्य् अर्धं वै पुरुषः सहस्रस्य यछन्त्य् अर्धम् इतरे पशवस् तस्माद् एतन् मध्यत उपदधात्य् अभिता इतराणि पशोः सवीर्यत्वायाथो सायतनत्वाय यं कामयेत पशुमान्त् स्याद् इति तस्य समीचीनानि पशुशीर्षाण्य् उपदध्यात् समीच एवास्मै पशून् उपदधाति पशुमान् भवत्य् अथ यं कामयेतापशुः स्याद् इति तस्य विषूचीनानि पशुशीर्षाण्य् उपदध्याद् विषूच एवास्मै पशून् उपदधात्य् अपशुर् भवत्य् एता वै साहस्रीर् इष्टकाः पश्विष्टकास् ताः सोमदक्षः कौश्रेयो विदांचकार ताः श्यापर्णायोपदधौ स सहस्रं पशून् प्राप प्र सहस्रं पशून् आप्नोति यस्यैता उपधीयन्ते यविष्ठो वै नामैषो ऽग्निस् तस्माच् चिन्वीतान्तरा न व्येतवै यद् वीयात् प्राणान् अस्य युवेतोत्सर्गैर् उपतिष्ठत आरण्यान् एव पशूञ् शुचम् अनूत्सृजति ॥
3.2.7.m:
Now, these are the Viśvajyotis [bricks].
In these worlds, indeed, he thereby places the luminous Agni,
and also for the support of the breaths.
Now, this one is marked with three lines.
These worlds, indeed, are marked with three lines.
These worlds alone he places.
Both the gods and the Asuras, indeed, placed this [brick].
The gods placed it with the mark on top;
the Asuras with the mark beneath.
Thence the gods prospered,
the Asuras perished.
One who has a rival, or one who may be dear to him, should place it with the mark on top.
He himself prospers; his rival perishes.
This indeed is the brick free from rivals.
Free from rivals becomes he who places it.
Moreover, this is indeed the mark of the gods;
he places the mark of the gods itself.
What clay remains over from the ukhā pot, of that he should make this [brick].
Thereby all his bricks belong to Agni.
Now, this is the tortoise.
Those [fires], indeed, are piled like burial mounds.
A living tortoise is to be placed;
thereby, indeed, this one is not a pile-layer on a burial mound;
thereby he is soaring upward.
This [tortoise], indeed, is the sap of the animals.
Seeing this sap, the animals wait upon him in yonder world.
He sets it facing westward,
for the animals wait upon the sap facing westward.
He sets it down with a verse addressed to Heaven and Earth,
for the animals wait along Heaven and Earth.
By means of the animals, indeed, he sets it in harmony.
"Agni should be piled on the navel of Viṣṇu," they say.
A mortar a span in measure is to be made;
so great, indeed, is Viṣṇu.
On the navel of Viṣṇu, indeed, Agni is thus piled.
"Agni should be piled on strength," they say.
The udumbara, indeed, is strength.
In that the mortar is made of udumbara wood,
Agni is thus piled on strength.
He sets it down with a verse addressed to Viṣṇu,
for the mortar belongs to Viṣṇu,
with his own deity indeed.
Now, this is the ukhā pot.
The vigour, the virility of the earth is thereby brought together.
Vigour, virility is thus placed in the middle of Agni;
moreover, in the middle light alone is piled.
If he should look down into it empty, the sacrificer would become hungry.
Then in that he looks down into it full,
thus indeed he does not become hungry.
It is to be filled with sand.
What sand is, that indeed is the ashes of Agni Vaiśvānara.
With his own ashes indeed he satisfies it.
It is to be filled with curd.
Curd, indeed, is strength.
Strength alone he secures.
It is to be filled with ghee.
This, indeed, is the dear body of Agni, namely ghee.
With his dear body alone he causes him to prosper.
It is to be filled with honey.
Truly in his offspring one fond of sweetness is born.
Deficient in faculties, indeed, are animal heads, unsuited for sacrifice, unholy.
In that he throws gold chips into the openings,
he enriches them with faculty, with virility;
he makes them holy, suited for sacrifice.
Man, indeed, is half of a thousand;
the other animals equal the [other] half.
Therefore he places this one in the middle,
the others around [it],
for the virility of the animal,
and also for its having a proper abode.
Whomever he might wish, "May he be rich in animals," of him he should place the animal heads facing one another;
facing one another indeed he places the animals for him;
he becomes rich in animals.
Then whomever he might wish, "May he be without animals," of him he should place the animal heads turned away;
turned away indeed he places the animals for him;
he becomes without animals.
These, indeed, are the bricks of a thousand, the animal bricks.
Somadakṣa Kauśreya knew them;
he placed them for Śyāparṇa;
he obtained a thousand animals.
He obtains a thousand animals for whom these are placed.
"The Youngest" indeed is this Agni by name;
from him one should pile [the fire].
One should not pass between [it and the bricks];
if he should pass between, he would sever his breaths.
He waits upon it with releases;
he releases the wild animals following after the burning heat.

3.2.8.s: puruṣaśīrṣam upadadhāty eṣa hi paśūnāṃ vīryavattamo vīryam asmin dadhāty ekam upadadhāty ekadhāsmin vīryaṃ dadhāti sauryā puruṣaśīrṣam abhijuhoti svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai saurī vā eṣā satī maitrāvaruṇy ahar vai mitro rātrir varuṇo 'horātrayor eva pratitiṣṭhaty ardhaṛcābhyāṃ juhotīyaṃ vā ardhaṛco 'sā ardhaṛco 'nayor eva pratitiṣṭhaty atha yad ekaya ṛcā dvir juhoti tasmād ekaḥ san puruṣo dvipād yad vā etat kiṃcākar yoniṃ vā etad vyakar yad etā apasyāḥ sādayati tasminn eva yonau reto dadhātīyaṃ vā abibhed agnir mātidhakṣyatīti saitā iṣṭakā apaśyad atho āhuḥ prajāpatir apaśyad iti tā upādhatte yad etā upadhīyante 'syā anatidāhāya yad id annam iti hovāceyaṃ ya etā upadadhātā ity annādo bhavati yasyaitā upadhīyante tasmād retasaḥ siktād eṣa paśuḥ saṃbhavati yad etāś chandasyāḥ paśavo vai chandāṃsi yad dakṣiṇata upadadhyād abhīpataḥ prajā varuṇo gṛhṇīyād atha yad uttarata upadadhāty apavāhata evāthaitāḥ prāṇabhṛtas tasmin paśau saṃbhūte prāṇaṃ cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ vācaṃ tāni dadhāty akṣṇayā sādayati paśuṃ vā etad ākramayati tasmāt paśavo 'kṣṇayāṅgāni praharanto yanti daśabhirdaśabhir vā atā iṣṭakābhir ṛṣaya ārdhnuvaṃs tā ṛddhīr ṛdhnoti yasyaitā upadhīyante 'thaitāḥ saṃyato reto vā etat sicyate yad agniś cīyate yad etā upadhīyante retasaḥ siktasya saṃyatyai lokaṃ pṛṇa chidraṃ pṛṇety eṣā vā achidreṣṭakā achidrā vā etayā citayaś cīyanta indrāgnī tvā bṛhaspatir ity ojo vai vīryam indrāgnī ojasā vā etad vīryeṇāgniś cīyate tā asya sūdadohasā iti paruṣiparuṣy eva rasaṃ dadhāti somaṃ śrīṇanti pṛśnayā ity annaṃ vai pṛśny annam evāvarunddhe janman devānāṃ viśā ity āha prajātyā eva triṣv ā rocane diva iti savanāni vai tṛṇi rocanāni savanacitam evainam akar anuṣṭub vā eṣā vāg vā anuṣṭup prāṇo vai vāg yad eṣā sarvā iṣṭakā anusaṃcarati tasmāt prāṇaḥ sarvāṇy aṅgāny anusaṃcaraty āgneyī vā eṣā varṇena svena vā etac chandasāgniś cīyate nādhvaryuḥ san nārttim ārchati ya evaṃ veda ||
3.2.8.d: पुरुषशीर्षम् उपदधात्य् एष हि पशूनां वीर्यवत्तमो वीर्यम् अस्मिन् दधात्य् एकम् उपदधात्य् एकधास्मिन् वीर्यं दधाति सौर्या पुरुषशीर्षम् अभिजुहोति स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य समष्ट्यै सौरी वा एषा सती मैत्रावरुण्य् अहर् वै मित्रो रात्रिर् वरुणो ऽहोरात्रयोर् एव प्रतितिष्ठत्य् अर्धऋचाभ्यां जुहोतीयं वा अर्धऋचो ऽसा अर्धऋचो ऽनयोर् एव प्रतितिष्ठत्य् अथ यद् एकय ऋचा द्विर् जुहोति तस्माद् एकः सन् पुरुषो द्विपाद् यद् वा एतत् किंचाकर् योनिं वा एतद् व्यकर् यद् एता अपस्याः सादयति तस्मिन्न् एव योनौ रेतो दधातीयं वा अबिभेद् अग्निर् मातिधक्ष्यतीति सैता इष्टका अपश्यद् अथो आहुः प्रजापतिर् अपश्यद् इति ता उपाधत्ते यद् एता उपधीयन्ते ऽस्या अनतिदाहाय यद् इद् अन्नम् इति होवाचेयं य एता उपदधाता इत्य् अन्नादो भवति यस्यैता उपधीयन्ते तस्माद् रेतसः सिक्ताद् एष पशुः संभवति यद् एताश् छन्दस्याः पशवो वै छन्दांसि यद् दक्षिणत उपदध्याद् अभीपतः प्रजा वरुणो गृह्णीयाद् अथ यद् उत्तरत उपदधात्य् अपवाहत एवाथैताः प्राणभृतस् तस्मिन् पशौ संभूते प्राणं चक्षुः श्रोत्रं वाचं तानि दधात्य् अक्ष्णया सादयति पशुं वा एतद् आक्रमयति तस्मात् पशवो ऽक्ष्णयाङ्गानि प्रहरन्तो यन्ति दशभिर्दशभिर् वा अता इष्टकाभिर् ऋषय आर्ध्नुवंस् ता ऋद्धीर् ऋध्नोति यस्यैता उपधीयन्ते ऽथैताः संयतो रेतो वा एतत् सिच्यते यद् अग्निश् चीयते यद् एता उपधीयन्ते रेतसः सिक्तस्य संयत्यै लोकं पृण छिद्रं पृणेत्य् एषा वा अछिद्रेष्टका अछिद्रा वा एतया चितयश् चीयन्त इन्द्राग्नी त्वा बृहस्पतिर् इत्य् ओजो वै वीर्यम् इन्द्राग्नी ओजसा वा एतद् वीर्येणाग्निश् चीयते ता अस्य सूददोहसा इति परुषिपरुष्य् एव रसं दधाति सोमं श्रीणन्ति पृश्नया इत्य् अन्नं वै पृश्न्य् अन्नम् एवावरुन्द्धे जन्मन् देवानां विशा इत्य् आह प्रजात्या एव त्रिष्व् आ रोचने दिव इति सवनानि वै तृणि रोचनानि सवनचितम् एवैनम् अकर् अनुष्टुब् वा एषा वाग् वा अनुष्टुप् प्राणो वै वाग् यद् एषा सर्वा इष्टका अनुसंचरति तस्मात् प्राणः सर्वाण्य् अङ्गान्य् अनुसंचरत्य् आग्नेयी वा एषा वर्णेन स्वेन वा एतच् छन्दसाग्निश् चीयते नाध्वर्युः सन् नार्त्तिम् आर्छति य एवं वेद ॥
3.2.8.m:
He places a human head.
For this is the most vigorous of animals.
He puts vigor into him.
He places one.
He puts vigor into him singly.
With a verse addressed to Sūrya he makes an oblation over the human head,
for the attainment of the heavenly world.
Being addressed to Sūrya, this [verse] is addressed to Mitra and Varuṇa.
Mitra is the day;
Varuṇa is the night.
He establishes himself in day and night.
With two half-verses he makes the oblation.
This [earth] is one half-verse;
yonder [sky] is the other half-verse.
In these two he establishes himself.
Now, in that with one ṛc verse he makes two oblations,
therefore a man, being one, is two-footed.
Whatever he has performed, a womb he has thereby prepared.
In that he sets down these water-bricks,
into that very womb he places seed.
This [earth] indeed feared:
"Agni will burn me overmuch."
She saw these bricks.
Moreover, they say:
"Prajāpati saw them."
He places them.
In that these are placed,
[it is] so that she will not be burnt overmuch.
"Whatever is food," so indeed she said, "[let him be] who shall place these."
He becomes an eater of food for whom these are placed.
From that seed poured, this animal comes into being, in that these are metre-bricks.
Metres indeed are animals.
If he were to place them on the south side, Varuṇa would seize the creatures headlong.
Then, in that he places them on the north side,
[it is] from flowing away.
Now, these are the breath-bearing [bricks].
When that animal has come into being, he places in him breath, eye, ear, and speech—those [faculties].
He sets them down diagonally;
he thereby makes the animal step forward.
Therefore animals move striking their limbs diagonally.
By tens each, indeed, the ṛṣis prospered through these bricks.
He prospers in those prosperings for whom these are placed.
Now, these are the joining [bricks].
Seed indeed is poured when Agni is piled.
In that these are placed,
[it is] for the holding together of the poured seed.
With "Fill the world, fill the gap,"
this indeed is the brick without a gap.
Without a gap, indeed, the layers are piled by means of it.
With "Indra and Agni, you, Bṛhaspati,"
force and vigor, indeed, are Indra and Agni.
With force, with vigor, indeed, Agni is thus piled.
With "Those of him with the bubbling drink,"
he puts sap in every joint.
With "They mix the Soma with the dappled one,"
food, indeed, is the dappled one.
Food alone he secures.
"At the birth of the gods, with the clan," he says,
for propagation alone.
With "In the three luminous realms of heaven,"
the three pressings, indeed, are the luminous realms.
He has thereby made him one who piles for the pressings.
This [verse], indeed, is an anuṣṭubh;
speech, indeed, is the anuṣṭubh;
breath, indeed, is speech.
In that this [formula] traverses all the bricks,
therefore breath traverses all the limbs.
It is addressed to Agni by its color.
With his own metre, indeed, Agni is thus piled.
Neither as Adhvaryu does he come to harm, who knows thus.

3.2.9.s: utsannayajño vā eṣa yad agniś cityaḥ ko ha tad veda yad etasya kriyate yan nāśvinau vai devānāṃ bhiṣajā akḷptasya kalpayitārau yad etā āśvinīr upadhīyante 'kḷptasya kḷptyai pañcopadadhāti pāṅkto yajño yāvān eva yajñas tam ālabdhātho yāvān eva yajñas tam acīkḷpad athaitā āśvinīr ṛtavyā anūpadhīyante retase vā etat siktāya ṛtūn upādhāt tasmāt sarveṣv ṛtuṣu reto hitaṃ tasmāt sarvān ṛtūn reto 'nuprajāyate 'thaitā ṛtavyā vāyavyā anūpadhīyante tasmāt sarvān ṛtūn vāyur anvāvarīvarty athaitā vāyavyā apasyā anūpadhīyante tasmāt paśavo nānāvratāḥ santo 'pa evābhi savratāś catasraḥ purastād upadadhāti caturvidhaṃ hi śiraḥ prāṇaś cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ vāṅ mūrdhanvatībhiḥ sādayati mūrdhanyo 'sānīti pañcapañcābhitā upadadhāti paśoḥ savīryatvāyātho sāyatanatvāya tasmāt paśuḥ paścād varīyāñ śroṇimattaras tasmād u prāṅ saṃhāna indrāgnī avyathamānām iṣṭakāṃ dṛṃhataṃ yuvam ity antarikṣaṃ vā eṣā citir antarikṣam imāḥ prajā indrāgnī vai devānām ojobhṛtav ojo vīryam indrāgnī ojo vā etad vīryaṃ madhyataḥ prajānāṃ dhīyate 'thaitā diśyā devā vai svargaṃ lokam āyaṃs te diśā ākramanta tā avlīyanta tā etābhir adṛṃhan yad etā upadhīyante diśāṃ dhṛtyai pañcopadadhāti pāṅkto yajño yāvān eva yajñas tam ālabdha daśaitāḥ purastāt sādayati daśākṣarā virāḍ virāṭ khalu vai cakṣur jyotiś chandasāṃ cakṣur vā etaj jyotiḥ purastāt paśor dadhāti tasmād idaṃ purastāc cakṣur atho annaṃ vai virāḍ annaṃ vā etan mukhato dadhāti mā chandaḥ pramā chandaḥ pratimā chandā itīyaṃ vai māntarikṣaṃ pramāsau pratimemān eva lokān upadhatte 'tho devachandasāni vā etāni devachandasāny evopadhatte dvādaśadvādaśābhitā upadadhāti tat ṣaṭtriṃśat ṣaṭtriṃśadakṣarā bṛhatī bṛhatī khalu vai chandasāṃ svārājyam ānaśe gachati svārājyaṃ yasyaitā upadhīyante paśavo vai bṛhatī paśavo madhyamā citis tasmād etasyāṃ cityām etā upadhīyanta ādityadhāmāno vā uttare prāṇā aṅgirodhāmāno 'dhare mūrdhāsi rāḍ iti ya uttare prāṇās tān etābhir dādhāra yantrī rāḍ iti ye 'dhare prāṇās tān etābhir dādhāra tad eṣāṃ vāvaitāḥ prāṇānāṃ vidhṛtyai samāvadbhājaḥ sādayati samāvadbhājo hīme prāṇāḥ prāṇānāṃ vidhṛtyai yaṃ dviṣyāt tasyākṣṇayā sādayet prāṇān asya mohayati pramāyuko bhavati mūrdhanvatībhiḥ sādayati mūrdhanyo 'sānīti ||
3.2.9.d: उत्सन्नयज्ञो वा एष यद् अग्निश् चित्यः को ह तद् वेद यद् एतस्य क्रियते यन् नाश्विनौ वै देवानां भिषजा अकॢप्तस्य कल्पयितारौ यद् एता आश्विनीर् उपधीयन्ते ऽकॢप्तस्य कॢप्त्यै पञ्चोपदधाति पाङ्क्तो यज्ञो यावान् एव यज्ञस् तम् आलब्धाथो यावान् एव यज्ञस् तम् अचीकॢपद् अथैता आश्विनीर् ऋतव्या अनूपधीयन्ते रेतसे वा एतत् सिक्ताय ऋतून् उपाधात् तस्मात् सर्वेष्व् ऋतुषु रेतो हितं तस्मात् सर्वान् ऋतून् रेतो ऽनुप्रजायते ऽथैता ऋतव्या वायव्या अनूपधीयन्ते तस्मात् सर्वान् ऋतून् वायुर् अन्वावरीवर्त्य् अथैता वायव्या अपस्या अनूपधीयन्ते तस्मात् पशवो नानाव्रताः सन्तो ऽप एवाभि सव्रताश् चतस्रः पुरस्ताद् उपदधाति चतुर्विधं हि शिरः प्राणश् चक्षुः श्रोत्रं वाङ् मूर्धन्वतीभिः सादयति मूर्धन्यो ऽसानीति पञ्चपञ्चाभिता उपदधाति पशोः सवीर्यत्वायाथो सायतनत्वाय तस्मात् पशुः पश्चाद् वरीयाञ् श्रोणिमत्तरस् तस्माद् उ प्राङ् संहान इन्द्राग्नी अव्यथमानाम् इष्टकां दृंहतं युवम् इत्य् अन्तरिक्षं वा एषा चितिर् अन्तरिक्षम् इमाः प्रजा इन्द्राग्नी वै देवानाम् ओजोभृतव् ओजो वीर्यम् इन्द्राग्नी ओजो वा एतद् वीर्यं मध्यतः प्रजानां धीयते ऽथैता दिश्या देवा वै स्वर्गं लोकम् आयंस् ते दिशा आक्रमन्त ता अव्लीयन्त ता एताभिर् अदृंहन् यद् एता उपधीयन्ते दिशां धृत्यै पञ्चोपदधाति पाङ्क्तो यज्ञो यावान् एव यज्ञस् तम् आलब्ध दशैताः पुरस्तात् सादयति दशाक्षरा विराड् विराट् खलु वै चक्षुर् ज्योतिश् छन्दसां चक्षुर् वा एतज् ज्योतिः पुरस्तात् पशोर् दधाति तस्माद् इदं पुरस्ताच् चक्षुर् अथो अन्नं वै विराड् अन्नं वा एतन् मुखतो दधाति मा छन्दः प्रमा छन्दः प्रतिमा छन्दा इतीयं वै मान्तरिक्षं प्रमासौ प्रतिमेमान् एव लोकान् उपधत्ते ऽथो देवछन्दसानि वा एतानि देवछन्दसान्य् एवोपधत्ते द्वादशद्वादशाभिता उपदधाति तत् षट्त्रिंशत् षट्त्रिंशदक्षरा बृहती बृहती खलु वै छन्दसां स्वाराज्यम् आनशे गछति स्वाराज्यं यस्यैता उपधीयन्ते पशवो वै बृहती पशवो मध्यमा चितिस् तस्माद् एतस्यां चित्याम् एता उपधीयन्त आदित्यधामानो वा उत्तरे प्राणा अङ्गिरोधामानो ऽधरे मूर्धासि राड् इति य उत्तरे प्राणास् तान् एताभिर् दाधार यन्त्री राड् इति ये ऽधरे प्राणास् तान् एताभिर् दाधार तद् एषां वावैताः प्राणानां विधृत्यै समावद्भाजः सादयति समावद्भाजो हीमे प्राणाः प्राणानां विधृत्यै यं द्विष्यात् तस्याक्ष्णया सादयेत् प्राणान् अस्य मोहयति प्रमायुको भवति मूर्धन्वतीभिः सादयति मूर्धन्यो ऽसानीति ॥
3.2.9.m:
A ruined sacrifice, indeed, is this, namely Agni to be piled.
Who knows that which is done of it, or which is not?
The two Aśvins, indeed, are the healers of the gods, the adjusters of the unadjusted.
In that these bricks addressed to the Aśvins are placed,
[it is] for the adjustment of the unadjusted.
He places five.
Fivefold is the sacrifice.
As great as the sacrifice is, so great he has taken hold of;
moreover, as great as the sacrifice is, so great he has adjusted.
Now, these season-bricks are placed following the ones addressed to the Aśvins.
For the seed poured, indeed, he thereby placed the seasons.
Therefore seed is deposited in all seasons;
therefore seed is born into all seasons.
Now, these bricks addressed to Vāyu are placed following the season-bricks.
Therefore Vāyu moves throughout all the seasons.
Now, these water-bricks are placed following those addressed to Vāyu.
Therefore animals, though having various observances, have the same observance towards water alone.
He places four in front.
For fourfold is the head:
breath, eye, ear, and speech.
He sets them down with [formulas] containing "head":
"May I be at the head."
He places five each on both sides,
for the vigor of the animal,
and also for its having an abode.
Therefore an animal is broader, with fuller hips, behind,
and therefore narrowing towards the front.
With "Indra and Agni, do you two firm the unswerving brick,"
the atmosphere, indeed, is this layer;
these creatures are the atmosphere.
Indra and Agni, indeed, are the bearers of force among the gods.
Force and vigor are Indra and Agni.
Force and vigor, indeed, are thereby placed in the middle of creatures.
Now, these are the directional [bricks].
The gods, indeed, went to the heavenly world.
They stepped across the directions;
they gave way.
They firmed them with these [bricks].
In that these are placed,
[it is] for the support of the directions.
He places five.
Fivefold is the sacrifice.
As great as the sacrifice is, so great he has taken hold of.
He sets down ten of these in front.
The virāj has ten syllables.
The virāj indeed is the eye, the light of the metres.
The eye, the light, indeed, he thereby places in front of the animal.
Therefore this eye is in front.
Moreover, the virāj is food;
food, indeed, he thereby places in the mouth.
"Mā is the metre;
pramā is the metre;
pratimā is the metre,"
this [earth] is mā;
the atmosphere is pramā;
yonder [sky] is pratimā.
These worlds alone he places.
Moreover, these are the divine metres;
the divine metres alone he places.
He places twelve each on both sides;
that makes thirty-six.
The bṛhatī has thirty-six syllables.
The bṛhatī indeed obtained sovereign rule among the metres.
He goes to sovereign rule for whom these are placed.
The bṛhatī is animals;
the middle layer is animals.
Therefore in this layer these are placed.
Having the domain of the Ādityas, indeed, are the upper breaths;
having the domain of the Aṅgirases are the lower.
With "Thou art the head, the ruler,"
what breaths are upper, those he has supported with these.
With "The supporter, the ruler,"
what breaths are lower, those he has supported with these.
Therefore these indeed are for the support of these breaths.
He sets them down having equal shares;
for having equal shares indeed are these breaths,
for the support of the breaths.
Against him whom he may hate, he should set them down diagonally;
he confuses his breaths;
he becomes liable to die.
He sets them down with [formulas] containing "head":
"May I be at the head."

3.2.10.s: trivṛdvatīṃ purastāt sādayati trivṛd vai yajñamukhaṃ mukhato vā etad yajñamukhaṃ dadāti saptadaśavatīṃ dakṣiṇato 'nnaṃ vai saptadaśo 'nnaṃ vā etad dakṣiṇato dadhāti tasmād dakṣiṇena hastenānnam adyate tasmād dakṣiṇo 'rdha ātmano vīryavattaras tasmād dakṣiṇam ardhaṃ vayāṃsy anuparyāvartante pañcadaśavatīm uttarata ojo vai pañcadaśa ojo vā etad uttarato dadhāty ekaviṃśavatīṃ paścāt pratiṣṭhityai trivṛdvatīṃ purastāt sādayati trivṛd vai yajñamukhaṃ mukhato vā etad yajñamukhaṃ dadhāti pañcadaśavatīṃ dakṣiṇataḥ sādayati saptadaśavatīm uttarataḥ pakṣayoḥ savīryatvāyātho sāyatanatvāya tasmād ubhābhyāṃ hastābhyām annam adyate 'tho vajro vai pañcadaśo vajreṇa vā etad yajamāno bhrātṛvyam ubhayato nirbhajaty ekaviṃśavatīṃ paścāt pratiṣṭhityai pratiṣṭhā hy ekaviṃśo 'rkasya vā eṣa vidhām anuvidhīyate 'nnam akro 'nnādo bhavati yasyaitā upadhīyante 'gner bhāgo 'si dīkṣāyā ādhipatyaṃ brahma spṛtaṃ trivṛt stomā iti spṛto vai nāmaitā iṣṭakā etābhir vai prajāpatir yadyad akāmayata tattad aspṛṇod yadyad evaitābhir yajamānaḥ kāmayate tattat spṛṇoty ekayāstuvata prajā adhīyanteti sṛṣṭayo vai nāmaitā iṣṭakā etābhir vai prajāpatir yadyad akāmayata tattad asṛjata yadyad evaitābhir yajamānaḥ kāmayate tattat sṛjate agne jātān praṇudā naḥ sapatnān iti purastāt sādayati ya eva jātāḥ sapatnās tān etayā praṇudate praty ajātān jātavedo nudasveti paścād ya eva jātāḥ sapatnās tān etayā pratinudate tad bhrātṛvyasya vā eṣa vinodaś catuścatvāriṃśī stomo varco draviṇam iti dakṣiṇataḥ sādayati ṣoḍaśī stomā ojo draviṇam ity uttarataś catuścatvāriṃśadakṣarā vai triṣṭub vajras triṣṭub vajraḥ ṣoḍaśī savyāpagrahaṇo vai vajro dakṣiṇāpraharaṇaḥ savyāpagrahaṇaṃ vā etad vajraṃ dakṣiṇāpraharaṇaṃ yajamāno bhrātṛvyāya praharati purīṣavatīṃ madhyataḥ sādayati purīṣam iva hīdaṃ madhyataḥ paśoḥ purīṣaṃ madhyam ātmanaḥ sātmānam evāgniṃ cinute 'thaitā virājo vāg vai virāṭ paśavo vā etā iṣṭakāḥ paśuṣu vā etad uttamāṃ vācaṃ dadhāti tasmāt paśumān uttamāṃ vācaṃ vadati || ity uparikāṇḍe dṛṣāno nāma dvitīyaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ ||
3.2.10.d: त्रिवृद्वतीं पुरस्तात् सादयति त्रिवृद् वै यज्ञमुखं मुखतो वा एतद् यज्ञमुखं ददाति सप्तदशवतीं दक्षिणतो ऽन्नं वै सप्तदशो ऽन्नं वा एतद् दक्षिणतो दधाति तस्माद् दक्षिणेन हस्तेनान्नम् अद्यते तस्माद् दक्षिणो ऽर्ध आत्मनो वीर्यवत्तरस् तस्माद् दक्षिणम् अर्धं वयांस्य् अनुपर्यावर्तन्ते पञ्चदशवतीम् उत्तरत ओजो वै पञ्चदश ओजो वा एतद् उत्तरतो दधात्य् एकविंशवतीं पश्चात् प्रतिष्ठित्यै त्रिवृद्वतीं पुरस्तात् सादयति त्रिवृद् वै यज्ञमुखं मुखतो वा एतद् यज्ञमुखं दधाति पञ्चदशवतीं दक्षिणतः सादयति सप्तदशवतीम् उत्तरतः पक्षयोः सवीर्यत्वायाथो सायतनत्वाय तस्माद् उभाभ्यां हस्ताभ्याम् अन्नम् अद्यते ऽथो वज्रो वै पञ्चदशो वज्रेण वा एतद् यजमानो भ्रातृव्यम् उभयतो निर्भजत्य् एकविंशवतीं पश्चात् प्रतिष्ठित्यै प्रतिष्ठा ह्य् एकविंशो ऽर्कस्य वा एष विधाम् अनुविधीयते ऽन्नम् अक्रो ऽन्नादो भवति यस्यैता उपधीयन्ते ऽग्नेर् भागो ऽसि दीक्षाया आधिपत्यं ब्रह्म स्पृतं त्रिवृत् स्तोमा इति स्पृतो वै नामैता इष्टका एताभिर् वै प्रजापतिर् यद्यद् अकामयत तत्तद् अस्पृणोद् यद्यद् एवैताभिर् यजमानः कामयते तत्तत् स्पृणोत्य् एकयास्तुवत प्रजा अधीयन्तेति सृष्टयो वै नामैता इष्टका एताभिर् वै प्रजापतिर् यद्यद् अकामयत तत्तद् असृजत यद्यद् एवैताभिर् यजमानः कामयते तत्तत् सृजते अग्ने जातान् प्रणुदा नः सपत्नान् इति पुरस्तात् सादयति य एव जाताः सपत्नास् तान् एतया प्रणुदते प्रत्य् अजातान् जातवेदो नुदस्वेति पश्चाद् य एव जाताः सपत्नास् तान् एतया प्रतिनुदते तद् भ्रातृव्यस्य वा एष विनोदश् चतुश्चत्वारिंशी स्तोमो वर्चो द्रविणम् इति दक्षिणतः सादयति षोडशी स्तोमा ओजो द्रविणम् इत्य् उत्तरतश् चतुश्चत्वारिंशदक्षरा वै त्रिष्टुब् वज्रस् त्रिष्टुब् वज्रः षोडशी सव्यापग्रहणो वै वज्रो दक्षिणाप्रहरणः सव्यापग्रहणं वा एतद् वज्रं दक्षिणाप्रहरणं यजमानो भ्रातृव्याय प्रहरति पुरीषवतीं मध्यतः सादयति पुरीषम् इव हीदं मध्यतः पशोः पुरीषं मध्यम् आत्मनः सात्मानम् एवाग्निं चिनुते ऽथैता विराजो वाग् वै विराट् पशवो वा एता इष्टकाः पशुषु वा एतद् उत्तमां वाचं दधाति तस्मात् पशुमान् उत्तमां वाचं वदति ॥ इत्य् उपरिकाण्डे दृषानो नाम द्वितीयः प्रपाठकः ॥
3.2.10.m:
He sets down [the brick] containing the trivṛt in front.
The trivṛt, indeed, is the mouth of the sacrifice.
At the mouth, indeed, he thereby places the mouth of the sacrifice.
[The brick] containing the saptadaśa on the south.
The saptadaśa, indeed, is food.
Food, indeed, he thereby places on the south.
Therefore food is eaten with the right hand.
Therefore the right half of the body is more vigorous.
Therefore birds turn around toward the right side.
[The brick] containing the pañcadaśa on the north.
Vigor, indeed, is the pañcadaśa.
Vigor, indeed, he thereby places on the north.
[The brick] containing the ekaviṃśa in the west,
for firm standing.
He sets down [the brick] containing the trivṛt in front.
The trivṛt, indeed, is the mouth of the sacrifice.
At the mouth, indeed, he thereby places the mouth of the sacrifice.
He sets down [the brick] containing the pañcadaśa on the south,
[the brick] containing the saptadaśa on the north,
for the equality of vigor of the two wings,
and also for having an abode.
Therefore food is eaten with both hands.
Moreover, the vajra, indeed, is the pañcadaśa.
With the vajra, indeed, the sacrificer thereby excludes his rival from both sides.
[The brick] containing the ekaviṃśa in the west,
for firm standing;
for the ekaviṃśa is a firm standing.
He is adjusted according to the rule of the arka.
Food is the arka.
He becomes an eater of food for whom these are placed.
"Agni's portion you are; of consecration the overlordship;
brahman is won;
the stoma is the trivṛt"—so [he says].
Won [spṛtā], indeed, by name are these bricks.
By means of these Prajāpati won whatever he desired.
Whatever the sacrificer desires, that he wins by means of these.
"With one they praised;
creatures were established"—so [he says].
Creations [sṛṣṭi], indeed, by name are these bricks.
By means of these Prajāpati created whatever he desired.
Whatever the sacrificer desires, that he creates by means of these.
"O Agni, repel our rivals that are born"—so he sets down in front.
Those rivals that are indeed born, them he repels with this one.
"Repel the unborn, O Jātavedas"—so in the west.
Those rivals that are indeed born, them he repels with this one.
That, indeed, is the repelling of this one's rival.
"The forty-fourfold stoma, brilliance, wealth"—so he sets down on the south.
"The sixteenfold stoma, vigor, wealth"—so on the north.
The triṣṭubh, indeed, has forty-four syllables.
The triṣṭubh is a vajra.
The sixteenfold [stoma] is a vajra.
With the left hand grasped, indeed, is the vajra struck with the right hand.
The vajra, grasped with the left hand and struck with the right hand, the sacrificer thereby hurls at his rival.
He sets down [the brick] containing loose earth in the middle.
Like loose earth, indeed, is this middle part of the animal.
Loose earth is the middle of the body.
He piles Agni along with his body.
Now, these are the virāj [bricks].
Speech, indeed, is the virāj.
Animals, indeed, are these bricks.
He thereby places the highest speech in the animals.
Therefore one who possesses animals speaks the highest speech.
Thus ends the second prapāṭhaka named Dṛṣāna in the upper kāṇḍa.

3.3.1.s: athaitāḥ stomabhāgā etāṃ vai bṛhaspatir asurebhyo 'dhi yajñasya pratiṣṭhām āharad yad etā upadhīyante yajñasya pratiṣṭhityai yajño vai devānām apadyata taṃ devāḥ stomabhāgābhiḥ pratyudastabhnuvan yad etā upadhīyante yajñasyottabdhyai prajāpatir vā etat pṛthivyā agnes tejaḥ samabharat tad agner evaitat tejaḥ saṃbhriyate 'thaitā nākasado nākaṃ ha vā asmā agniṃ cikyānāya bhavati na vai tatra kiṃ cana jagmuṣe kaṃ tasmān nākasado nākasatsu pañcacūḍā adhyupadadhāti svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyay eṣa ha tv eva yajamānaḥ patnībhir agnināmuṣmiṃl loke samyaṅ yasyaitā upadhīyante 'tho madhye jyotir eva cīyata etā vā amuṣmiṃl loke yajamānasya patnīs tasmād agnicitā strī nopetyerṣyā hi sā paścāt prācīm uttamām upadadhāti paścād dhy etaṃ prācī patny anvāste 'thaitāḥ kḷptayaḥ prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tā enaṃ sṛṣṭā atyamanyanta sa prajāpatir etā iṣṭakā apaśyat tā upādhatta tato vā akalpata yad etā upadhīyante prajānāṃ kḷptyay athaitā vṛṣṭisanayo vṛṣṭir vai devebhyo 'nnādyam apākrāmat tata idaṃ sarvam aśuṣyat te devāḥ prajāpatim evopādhāvan sa prajāpatir etā iṣṭakā apaśyat tā upādhatta tebhyo vṛṣṭim annādyam avārunddha yad etā upadhīyante vṛṣṭyā annādyasyāvaruddhyay āvapanaṃ vā uttamā citir anyāanyā iṣṭakā upadadhāty anyānanyān evāsmai paśūn prajanayati prāṇo vai svayamātṛṇṇāyur vāyavyā samīcī upadadhāty āyuś caiva prāṇaṃ ca sayujā akar atho samīcīnābhyāṃ hy āyuṣā ca prāṇena ca bhuñjate prāṇo vai svayamātṛṇṇā tām uttamām upadadhāty uttamaṃ hy āyur yad anyām uttarām upadadhyāt prāṇam asyāpidadhyāt pramāyukaḥ syāt tasmāt tām uttamām upadadhāty uttamaṃ hy āyuḥ ||
3.3.1.d: अथैताः स्तोमभागा एतां वै बृहस्पतिर् असुरेभ्यो ऽधि यज्ञस्य प्रतिष्ठाम् आहरद् यद् एता उपधीयन्ते यज्ञस्य प्रतिष्ठित्यै यज्ञो वै देवानाम् अपद्यत तं देवाः स्तोमभागाभिः प्रत्युदस्तभ्नुवन् यद् एता उपधीयन्ते यज्ञस्योत्तब्ध्यै प्रजापतिर् वा एतत् पृथिव्या अग्नेस् तेजः समभरत् तद् अग्नेर् एवैतत् तेजः संभ्रियते ऽथैता नाकसदो नाकं ह वा अस्मा अग्निं चिक्यानाय भवति न वै तत्र किं चन जग्मुषे कं तस्मान् नाकसदो नाकसत्सु पञ्चचूडा अध्युपदधाति स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य समष्ट्यय् एष ह त्व् एव यजमानः पत्नीभिर् अग्निनामुष्मिंल् लोके सम्यङ् यस्यैता उपधीयन्ते ऽथो मध्ये ज्योतिर् एव चीयत एता वा अमुष्मिंल् लोके यजमानस्य पत्नीस् तस्माद् अग्निचिता स्त्री नोपेत्येर्ष्या हि सा पश्चात् प्राचीम् उत्तमाम् उपदधाति पश्चाद् ध्य् एतं प्राची पत्न्य् अन्वास्ते ऽथैताः कॢप्तयः प्रजापतिः प्रजा असृजत ता एनं सृष्टा अत्यमन्यन्त स प्रजापतिर् एता इष्टका अपश्यत् ता उपाधत्त ततो वा अकल्पत यद् एता उपधीयन्ते प्रजानां कॢप्त्यय् अथैता वृष्टिसनयो वृष्टिर् वै देवेभ्यो ऽन्नाद्यम् अपाक्रामत् तत इदं सर्वम् अशुष्यत् ते देवाः प्रजापतिम् एवोपाधावन् स प्रजापतिर् एता इष्टका अपश्यत् ता उपाधत्त तेभ्यो वृष्टिम् अन्नाद्यम् अवारुन्द्ध यद् एता उपधीयन्ते वृष्ट्या अन्नाद्यस्यावरुद्ध्यय् आवपनं वा उत्तमा चितिर् अन्याअन्या इष्टका उपदधात्य् अन्यानन्यान् एवास्मै पशून् प्रजनयति प्राणो वै स्वयमातृण्णायुर् वायव्या समीची उपदधात्य् आयुश् चैव प्राणं च सयुजा अकर् अथो समीचीनाभ्यां ह्य् आयुषा च प्राणेन च भुञ्जते प्राणो वै स्वयमातृण्णा ताम् उत्तमाम् उपदधात्य् उत्तमं ह्य् आयुर् यद् अन्याम् उत्तराम् उपदध्यात् प्राणम् अस्यापिदध्यात् प्रमायुकः स्यात् तस्मात् ताम् उत्तमाम् उपदधात्य् उत्तमं ह्य् आयुः ॥
3.3.1.m:
Now, these are the Stomabhāgā [bricks].
Bṛhaspati, indeed, brought this firm standing of the sacrifice away from the Asuras.
In that these are placed,
[it is] for the firm standing of the sacrifice.
The sacrifice, indeed, fell down from the gods.
The gods propped it up with the Stomabhāgā [bricks].
In that these are placed,
[it is] for the propping up of the sacrifice.
Prajāpati, indeed, thereby brought together the fiery brilliance of Agni from the earth.
Thereby this fiery brilliance of Agni is brought together.
Now, these are the Nākasad [bricks].
A vault [nāka], indeed, comes to be for him who has piled the fire;
there is no lack of pleasure [akam] for one who has gone thither.
Therefore they are Nākasad [vault-sitting bricks].
Upon the Nākasad bricks he places the Pañcacūḍā [five-crested bricks],
for the attainment of the heavenly world.
He alone, indeed, as sacrificer, is united in yonder world with his wives and with Agni, for whom these are placed.
Moreover, light alone is piled in the middle.
These, indeed, are the wives of the sacrificer in yonder world.
Therefore a woman should not be approached by one who has piled the fire-altar;
for she is jealousy.
In the west, facing east, he places the highest one;
for in the west, facing east, the wife sits behind him.
Now, these are the Kḷpti [adjustment bricks].
Prajāpati created creatures.
Having been created, they despised him.
Prajāpati saw these bricks;
he placed them.
Then indeed it was adjusted.
In that these are placed,
[it is] for the adjustment of creatures.
Now, these are the Vṛṣṭisani [rain-winning bricks].
Rain, proper food, indeed went away from the gods.
Then this whole world dried up.
The gods ran up to Prajāpati.
Prajāpati saw these bricks;
he placed them.
He gained rain, proper food, for them.
In that these are placed,
[it is] for the gaining of rain, of proper food.
A receptacle of sowing, indeed, is the highest layer.
He places different bricks;
he propagates different animals for him.
The breath, indeed, is the naturally perforated [brick]; life is the one addressed to Vāyu.
He places the two facing each other.
He has yoked together life and breath;
moreover, with life and with breath, which are facing each other, they enjoy.
The breath, indeed, is the naturally perforated [brick].
He places it as the highest;
for life is the highest.
If he were to place another above it, he would cover his breath, [and] he would be liable to die.
Therefore he places it as the highest;
for life is the highest.

3.3.2.s: athaiṣā chandaścitiś chandāṃsi vai devānāṃ vāmaṃ paśavaś chandāṃsy evaitayā vāmaṃ paśūn yajamāno 'varunddha etāṃ vai yajñasenaś caitra upadadhe sa ānardha ṛdhnoti ya etām upadhatte gāyatrībhiḥ purastāt sādayati tejo vai gāyatrī brahmavarcasaṃ teja eva brahmavarcasam avarunddhe tisra upadadhāti trivṛd dhy agnir mūrdhanvatībhiḥ sādayati mūrdhanyo 'sānīti triṣṭubbhir dakṣiṇata ojo vai vīryaṃ triṣṭub oja eva vīryam avarunddhe jagatībhiḥ paścād jāgatāḥ paśavaḥ paśūn evāvarunddhe 'nuṣṭubbhir uttarato 'nuṣṭub vai sarvāṇi chandāṃsi sarvāṇy evāsya chandāṃsy upahitāni bhavanty atha paṅktīr atha bṛhatīr athoṣṇiho 'tha kakubho 'tha virāja evam asya yathāpūrvaṃ chandāṃsy upahitāni bhavanti dvipadā uttamāḥ sādayati dvipād yajamānaḥ pratiṣṭhityai chandāṃsi vai devānāṃ vāmaṃ paśavo yajamānāyatanaṃ vā āhavanīyo bhrātṛvyāyatanaṃ dhiṣṇyā yat paścopadadhyād bhrātṛvyāyatane vāmaṃ paśūn dadhyād atha yat pura upadadhāti yajamānāyatane vā etad vāmaṃ paśūn dadhāty aṣṭopadadhāty aṣṭākṣarā gāyatrī gāyatro 'gnir yāvān evāgnis taṃ cinute 'ṣṭau gāyatrībhiḥ purastād bahiḥpavamānasyopadadhyād yady enaṃ bhrātṛvyo 'tīva syād ekādaśa triṣṭubbhiḥ purastān mādhyaṃdinasya pavamānasya dvādaśa jagatībhiḥ purastād ārbhavasya pavamānasyaitā eva paścāt pavāmanānām upadadhyād yady enaṃ bhrātṛvyo 'tīva syāt prāṇo vai pavāmāno 'gnes tejaḥ pavamānas tejasā vā etad yajamāno bhrātṛvyaṃ prabhūtaṃ praṇudate tejasā pratinudate tejasā vinudate tad bhrātṛvyasya vā eṣa vinodo jānudaghnaṃ prathamaṃ cinvānaś cinvīta gāyatrīcitaṃ nābhidaghnaṃ dvitīyaṃ cinvānaś cinvīta triṣṭupcitaṃ cubukadaghnaṃ tṛtīyaṃ cinvānaś cinvīta jagaccitaṃ yaj jyāyāṃsaṃ citvā kanīyāṃsaṃ cinvīta kanīyāṃsaṃ yajñakratum upeyāt kanīyasīṃ prajāṃ kanīyasaḥ paśūn kanīyo 'nnādyaṃ pāpīyānt syād atha yat kanīyāṃsaṃ citvā jyāyāṃsaṃ cinute jyāyāṃsam eva yajñakratum upaiti bhūyasīṃ prajāṃ bhūyasaḥ paśūn bhūyo 'nnādyaṃ vasīyān bhavaty eṣā vā agner uttaravatī nāma citir uttaramuttaraṃ śvaḥśvaḥ śreyān bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
